# 1 Introduction


## 1.1 About this plan

Willoughby Development Control Plan (Willoughby DCP) provides guidelines and controls for developments within the Willoughby local government area. This DCP repeals DCP 2006 pursuant to section 16 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2021. It supports the objectives and planning provisions in Willoughby Local Environmental Plan (Willoughby LEP).

All development applications submitted to Willoughby City Council are assessed in line with the performance criteria, development controls and other relevant provisions in this plan.

Each application is also assessed on the individual merits of the proposed development. A proposal may comply with the development controls in this plan but this does not necessarily ensure it will be approved.

This plan is in line with Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 (part 3, section 3.43) and Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2000 (part 3).


## 1.2 Aim

The aim of this part is to give an overview of the different sections of Willoughby DCP.


## 1.3 Objectives

This part:

- advises when a development application is needed and the supporting information required as part of the application
- explains how this plan relates to other state and local plans, policies, and guidelines
- details the other parts of Willoughby DCP.

# 2 Framework of this plan


## 2.1 Land covered by Willoughby DCP

This plan applies to all land and development within the City of Willoughby local government area.


## 2.2 Terms and definitions

The terms 'this plan', 'the plan', 'DCP' and 'Willoughby DCP' refer to this document, Willoughby Development Control Plan.

The terms 'Willoughby LEP' and 'the LEP' refer to Willoughby Local Environmental Plan.

The terms 'we', 'us' and 'our' in this plan refer to the local government authority 'Willoughby City Council', which serves the City of Willoughby local government area.

The terms 'local area' and 'our area' refer to the City of Willoughby local government area.

The term 'Council' refers to the elected group of councillors for Willoughby City Council.


<!-- SRC: 00-part-a-overview-of-wdcp-2023.pdf | PAGE: 6 -->

An 'Authorised Officer' is a Council employee that has been granted delegated authority to make decisions on behalf of Council.

Other definitions and meanings of the terms used in this document are the same as the terms listed in the dictionary under Willoughby LEP and any other definitions under relevant state plans, policies or codes.


## 2.3 Parts of this plan

This plan is divided into 12 parts, A to L.


### 2.3.1 Part A: Overview of Willoughby DCP

This part outlines the DCP and includes a link to the development application process. It explains the relationship of this plan to other state and local plans, policies and guidelines.


### 2.3.2 Part B: Residential Development

This part includes these sections and attachments:

- Section 1 is an introduction with the aims and objectives for this part.
- Section 2 provides the performance criteria for all types of residential accommodation.
- Section 3 includes controls for 'minor' developments such as dwelling houses and dual occupancies.
- Section 4 provides guidelines and controls for major residential development, such as residential flat buildings, manor houses, and apartments associated with shop top housing and mixed use developments.
- Section 5 provides specific controls for additional permitted land uses such as secondary dwellings, bed and breakfast accommodation, boarding houses and 'built-to-rent' housing.
- Section 6 provides specific controls for child care centres in residential areas.
- Section 7 provides further controls for any future development of specific sites and areas.
- Attachment 1 includes a compliance checklist table for controls in the R2 zone.
- Attachment 2 includes a compliance checklist table for controls relating to manor houses, attached dwellings and multi dwelling housing in the R3 zone.
Attachment 3 includes a compliance checklist of controls for residential development of three or more storeys and four or more dwellings and the residential components of shop top and mixed-use developments in the R3 and R4 zones, Further controls apply to developments in R2 zones that are within a heritage conservation area. Part H details these controls.


### 2.3.3 Part C: Development in C4 Environmental Living Zone

This part includes specific performance criteria and controls to provide for low impact development on land close to foreshore areas and environmentally sensitive locations.

Further controls apply to developments in C4 zones that are within a heritage conservation area. Part H details these controls.


<!-- SRC: 00-part-a-overview-of-wdcp-2023.pdf | PAGE: 7 -->


### 2.3.4 Part D: Commercial Development

This part includes performance criteria and controls for all types of commercial and nonresidential development. This includes the commercial components of shop top housing and mixed use developments and placed based plans.

Further controls may apply to commercial and retail premises in a heritage conservation area. Part H details these controls.


### 2.3.5 Part E: Industrial Development

This part includes guidelines and controls for industrial development and other land uses permitted in the industrial zones.


### 2.3.6 Part F: Transport and Parking Management

This part applies to all developments. It provides advice and controls for traffic management, off-street car parking, bicycle parking and end-of-trip facilities, loading and unloading facilities, and other traffic and transport related matters.

It is informed by Willoughby Integrated Transport Strategy 2036. See willoughby.nsw.gov.au.


### 2.3.7 Part G: Vegetation Management

This part applies to any development that involves the removal of trees or vegetation.

It is made under Part 2.2 of State Environmental Planning Policy (Biodiversity and Conservation) 2021 . See State Environmental Planning Policy (Biodiversity and Conservation) 2021 - NSW Legislation

It is supported by our Vegetation Management Guidelines. See willoughby.nsw.gov.au.


### 2.3.8 Part H: Heritage Items and Heritage Conservation Areas

This part is subject to Clause 5.10 (Heritage conservation) of Willoughby LEP . The clause deals with the environmental heritage of Willoughby, including heritage items, heritage conservation areas, conservation of archaeological sites, and conservation of Aboriginal objects and Aboriginal places of heritage significance.

Heritage items and an archaeological site are identified in Schedule 5 of Willoughby LEP. Heritage conservation areas are shown in the heritage maps accompanying the LEP.

Part H includes controls and measures to conserve and protect the heritage values of existing dwellings and commercial/retail buildings. It also has controls to ensure any new development is in keeping and sympathetic to the character of the particular heritage conservation area.

Any residential or commercial/retail development in a heritage conservation area must also consider the performance criteria and controls in parts B, C and D of this plan. If there is any inconsistency with the controls under parts B, C and D of the Willoughby DCP, the controls under Part H prevail.

The LEP does not identify Aboriginal objects or Aboriginal places of heritage significance. If a development is likely to disturb any natural bushland or geological features, applicants should contact Willoughby City Council to determine if a site comprises or is in proximity to an Aboriginal object or Aboriginal place of heritage significance.


<!-- SRC: 00-part-a-overview-of-wdcp-2023.pdf | PAGE: 8 -->


### 2.3.9 Part I: Stormwater Management

This part provides advice and controls for stormwater management. It applies to proposals for developments that will increase the amount of impervious surface areas and that need to provide an onsite detention (OSD) system and/or rainwater reuse tank.


### 2.3.10 Part J: Building Sustainability

This part provides advice and controls to achieve energy efficient and environmentally sustainable buildings. It applies to any application for new development or significant alterations and additions. These controls ensure best practice sustainability measures are included in the design and construction of buildings.


### 2.3.11 Part K: Development near Lane Cove Tunnel Ventilation Stacks

This part applies to any new development within an 800m radius of the ventilation stacks in Sirius Road, Lane Cove West and Marsden Street, Artarmon.


### 2.3.12 Part L: Place Based Plans

This part provides specific guidelines and controls for development in the Chatswood Central Business District (CBD) and the following local centres:

- Artarmon
- Castlecrag
- North Willoughby
- High Street
- Naremburn
- Northbridge
- Penshurst Street
- Willoughby South.
This part also provides guidelines and controls for specific sites including in the Chatswood CBD and sites in or near local centres. The performance criteria and controls for residential and commercial development in parts B and D of this plan also apply to these place based plans.

If there is inconsistency with the controls in Parts B and D, the controls under Part L prevail.


# 3 Existing use rights

The existing use provisions under Division 4.11 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 and Part 5 of the Environmental Planning Regulations 2000 apply to any development that is not a permissible land use within a particular zone. This includes dwellings that are not permissible in the R3 Medium Density Residential or R4 High Density Residential Zones.

An application for change of use, alterations or extensions, or rebuilding of a non-conforming existing use, must address the standards for that type of development that would otherwise be permissible in a zone. The application will be assessed against the provisions in this plan for that type of development.


<!-- SRC: 00-part-a-overview-of-wdcp-2023.pdf | PAGE: 9 -->

The onus of proof is on the owner of the subject property to establish that 'existing use rights' apply in line with Clause 4.65 of the Act and Section 39 of the Regulations.


# 4 The development application process

The forms, checklists and other details needed as part of a development application and modification application are at willoughby.nsw.gov.au.

Willoughby City Council offers applicants a pre-lodgement meeting for development applications. After the meeting we provide a written response.

Applicants can contact our Customer Services division for an appointment and the current fee for the pre-lodgement meeting.

The legal framework to lodge, assess and determine applications for development approval is in Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 (part 4, development assessment and consent). The Act is available at legislation.nsw.gov.au.


# 5 Notifications of development

Depending on the type and scale of development, a proposal may be notified and advertised before Willoughby City Council assesses and determines the application.

Our community participation process and practices in the planning process are set out in Willoughby Community Participation Plan. Part D of the plan details the development application notification process.

Willoughby Community Participation Plan is at willoughby.nsw.gov.au.


# 6 Related plans, policies and guidelines


## 6.1 Willoughby Local Environmental Plan

Willoughby LEP is the statutory planning instrument for land and development in the Willoughby local government area.

It provides the objectives and land use tables for residential, business, industrial, special purpose, and environmental protection zones. Each category identifies land uses that are permitted without consent, permitted with consent, and prohibited. It includes additional permitted uses under Schedule 1 for certain sites.

It also provides the principal development standards, including height of buildings, landscaped area and floor space ratio (FSR) controls.

This plan, Willoughby DCP, provides guidelines and controls that support Willoughby LEP.


## 6.2 Willoughby City Local Strategic Planning Statement

This is a 20-year vision for land use in the Willoughby local government area. It gives effect to the Greater Sydney Commission's North District Plan and informs this plan and Willoughby LEP.

It provides information on:

- the existing and future character of Willoughby

<!-- SRC: 00-part-a-overview-of-wdcp-2023.pdf | PAGE: 10 -->

- future housing, jobs, and services
- future infrastructure requirements such as community facilities and transport initiatives
- protection of the environmental and heritage values, areas, and items.
The Willoughby City Local Strategic Planning Statement is at willoughby.nsw.gov.au.


## 6.3 State environmental planning policies

The NSW Government is responsible for many environmental planning policies (SEPPs). Some of these policies have inconsistent and overlapping controls.

The main polices and codes relevant to our local government area are listed below.

6.3.1 State Environmental Planning Policy (Exempt and Complying Development Codes) 2008

The provisions in this policy allow some structures and land uses to be carried out without approval, subject to certain development standards and other provisions. They also allow some business and building identification signs to be erected without approval.

The policy includes several codes that allow certain works, change of use and subdivision to be done as complying development.

These codes are relevant to our local government area:

- Housing Code (Part 3)
- Low Rise Housing Diversity Code (Part 3B)
- Housing Alterations Code (Part 4)
- General Development Code (Part 4A)
- Commercial and Industrial Alterations Code (Part 5)
- Industrial and Business Buildings Code (Part 5A)
- Container Recycling Facilities Code (Part 5B)
- Subdivisions Code (Part 6)
- Demolition Code (Part 7)
- Fire Safety Code (Part 8)
Willoughby DCP includes many of the same controls so that it is generally in line with these codes.

A development application (DA) is required if a proposed development does not satisfy all the criteria under the codes.

The Codes SEPP is at State Environmental Planning Policy (Exempt and Complying Development Codes) 2008.


### 6.3.2 State Environmental Planning Policy (Sustainable Buildings ) 2022

Under this policy an application for residential accommodation must include a BASIX certificate, which has a list of commitments to achieve a prescribed level of sustainable residential development.


<!-- SRC: 00-part-a-overview-of-wdcp-2023.pdf | PAGE: 11 -->

Willoughby City Council cannot approve a development application for residential development that exceeds $50,000, or a swimming pool or spa with a volume exceeding 40,000 litres, if it does not achieve the minimum BASIX score.

Detailed information on BASIX is available from the Department of Planning and Environment at planningportal.nsw.gov.au.

The BASIX SEPP is at State Environmental Planning Policy (Sustainable Buildings) 2022.


### 6.3.3 State Environmental Planning Policy (Planning Systems) 2021

The Planning Systems SEPP:

- identifies state or regionally significant development, state-significant infrastructure, and critical state-significant infrastructure
- provides for consideration of development delivery plans by local Aboriginal land councils in planning assessment
- allows the planning secretary to elect to be the concurrence authority for certain development that requires concurrence under nominated state environmental planning policies.
The Planning Policy SEPP is at State Environmental Planning Policy (Planning Systems) 2021 - NSW Legislation


### 6.3.4 State Environmental Planning Policy (Biodiversity and Conservation) 2021

The Biodiversity and Conservation SEPP includes:

- planning rules and controls for the clearing of native vegetation in NSW on land zoned for urban and environmental purposes that is not linked to a development application
- provisions seeking to protect and preserve bushland within public open space zones and reservations
- provisions to manage and improve environmental outcomes for Sydney Harbour and its tributaries
The Biodiversity and Conservation SEPP is at State Environmental Planning Policy (Biodiversity and Conservation) 2021 - NSW Legislation


### 6.3.5 State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021

The Resilience and Hazards SEPP includes provisions:

- for land use planning within the coastal zone, consistent with the Coastal Management Act 2016
- to manage hazardous and offensive development
- to provide a state-wide planning framework for the remediation of contaminated land and to minimise the risk of harm.
The Resilience and Hazards SEPP is at State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021 - NSW Legislation


<!-- SRC: 00-part-a-overview-of-wdcp-2023.pdf | PAGE: 12 -->


### 6.3.6 State Environmental Planning Policy (Transport and Infrastructure) 2021

The Transport and Infrastructure SEPP includes provisions:

- for infrastructure in NSW, such as hospitals, roads, railways, emergency services, water supply and electricity delivery
- for child-care centres, schools, TAFEs and universities
The Transport and Infrastructure SEPP is at State Environmental Planning Policy (Transport and Infrastructure) 2021 - NSW Legislation


### 6.3.7 State Environmental Planning Policy (Industry and Employment) 2021

The Industry and Employment SEPP includes provisions:

- for advertising and signage in NSW
The Industry and Employment SEPP is at State Environmental Planning Policy (Industry and Employment) 2021 - NSW Legislation


### 6.3.8 State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021

The Housing SEPP includes provisions relating to:

- boarding houses
- build-to-rent housing
- seniors housing
- group homes
- retention of existing affordable rental housing
- secondary dwellings (granny flats)
- social and affordable housing
- short-term rental accommodation
- residential apartment development.
The Housing SEPP is at State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021 - NSW Legislation


## 6.4 Other state and local plans, policies and guidelines

These polices and guides also apply to residential development:

- Apartment Design Guide, NSW Department of Planning and Environment, July 2015
More details on these are in Part B (Residential Development) of this plan.

Other plans, policies and guidelines may apply to specific or different types of developments. These can be found at legislation.nsw.gov.au or on the NSW planning portal.

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part B: Residential Development 2023


# 1 Introduction

This part of Willoughby Development Control Plan includes guidelines and controls for low, medium and high density residential development. It also includes controls for the residential components of shop top housing and mixed use developments in the business zones.

Further controls apply to residential development in heritage conservation areas (Part H) and dwellings in the C4 Environmental Living Zone (Part C) in this plan.


## 1.1 Aim

This part aims to provide a consistent and equitable approach to residential development outcomes. It incorporates the provisions of relevant state planning polices and guidelines and current best practice provisions into local planning controls for the City of Willoughby area.


## 1.2 Objectives


### This part:


## 1.3 Checklist for development applications

There are three compliance checklists for different types of residential development in Attachments 1, 2 and 3 of this part. These cover:

- minor residential development, including single dwellings and dual occupancies in the R2 zone (Attachment 1)
- manor houses, attached dwellings and multi dwelling housing in the R3 zone (Attachment 2)
- residential flat buildings, the residential component of shop top housing, and mixed use developments comprising three or more storeys and four or more dwellings (Attachment 3).
A development application for residential development must include the relevant compliance checklist.

# 2 Performance criteria


## 2.1 General performance criteria

These performance criteria apply to all developments for residential accommodation.

A proposed development will generally be seen as meeting the performance criteria for design and amenity issues if it complies with:

- this part and other parts of this control plan
- the relevant provisions of the state planning policies, guidelines
- Willoughby Local Environmental Plan (Willoughby LEP).
Any variation of the controls must be justified. It must consider the general performance criteria below and the provisions in other relevant plans, policies and guidelines.

### 2.1.11 Urban heat

The objective is to reduce temperatures and create a resilient framework to mitigate the extreme impacts of urban heat by including appropriate measures to improve the health, comfort and wellbeing of residents. To reduce the impacts of urban heat island effects the development should:


### 2.1.12 View sharing

The objective is to limit the extent and impact on existing views. Developments should, as far as reasonably possible:


### 2.1.13 Natural heritage

The objective is to preserve and protect significant trees/vegetation and other natural features such as rock outcrops.

Willoughby City Council has a natural heritage register which identifies items of natural heritage, including items on private properties.

A proponent should access the register to determine if the subject property has significant trees or other natural features that should be preserved and protected from any proposed development.

The register is at willoughby.nsw.gov.au/Environment/Bushland-and-Wildlife/Natural-HeritageRegister.


### 2.1.14 Storage areas and plant rooms

The objective is to reduce excessive areas nominated as storage area and/or plant rooms, which could be subsequently used for habitable purposes. The additional floor area often contributes to excessive excavation and additional bulk.

# 3 Minor developments

Minor residential developments include construction of and alterations and additions to:

Notes:

- A boarding house is required to be maintained and operated in a single entity; strata subdivision is not permitted.
- Depending on the size and scale, and any likely impacts, an authorised officer may determine that a proposal is seen as 'major' development.

## 3.1 Controls for development in the R2 zone

This plan aims to provide a consistent approach in assessing development applications in the R2 zone. Unless otherwise stated, this plan adopts the relevant controls from State Environmental Planning Policy (Exempt and Complying Development Codes) 2008 (Codes SEPP). These SEPP controls include:

- Housing Code (Part 3)
- Low Rise Housing Diversity Code on certain dual occupancies (Part 3B)
- Housing Alterations Code (Part 4).
Some of the notable exceptions from the Code SEPP controls for development in the R2 zone include the floor space ratio (FSR), landscaped area, number of car parking spaces and certain additional controls for Heritage Conservation Areas.

Notes:

- The required number of car parking spaces are provided in Part F (Transport and Car Parking Management) of this plan.
- The additional Heritage controls are provided in Part H (Heritage Items and Heritage Conservation areas) of this plan.
- Site constraints may preclude a development achieving full compliance and/or the most desirable amenity outcomes. Any variation of the numerical controls must be justified, considering the performance criteria in Section 2.1 of this part and other relevant plans, policies and guidelines.
- Any development for attached or detached dual occupancies must satisfy the objectives and design criteria in the Low Rise Housing Diversity Design Guide, Department of Planning Industry and Environment, July 2020. This is at planning.nsw.gov.au

## 3.2 Controls for landscaping

The minimum landscaped area controls are:

| Site area (m 2 )   | Minimum landscaped area (m 2 )   |
|--------------------|----------------------------------|
| Under 200          | 0.25 x site area                 |
| 200 - 400          | (0.35 x site area) less 20       |
| 401 - 600          | (0.6 x site area) less 120       |
| 601 - 1000         | (0.525 x site area) less75       |
| 1001 - 1500        | (0.6 x site area)less 150        |
| Over 1500          | 0.5 x site area                  |


### Note:

- The minimum landscaped area includes all deep soil zones and soft landscaped areas (the minimum dimension to be included in the deep soil zone and soft landscaped area calculation is 1m).
- Deep soil zones are areas that are free of sub-ground structures such as basement car parking areas, detention tanks or the like.
- Soft landscaped areas are areas that comprise a minimum depth of 600mm to enable the establishment of vegetation, including shrubs and small trees.

### Additional landscaping controls are:

-  70% of the area forward of the building line to the primary road where a site has a width, measured at the building line, of at least 18m.
-  50% of the area forward of the building line to the primary road where a site has a width, measured at the building line, of less than 18m.

## 3.3 Controls for ancillary structures

This plan adopts the development standards in the Housing Code (Codes SEPP, Part 3) for attached and detached balconies, decks, patios, terraces and verandahs located at the side and rear of a dwelling.

Any variation to these controls must meet these performance criteria:

Note:

- Greater emphasis is placed on maintaining visual privacy to living areas and private open spaces than for non-living rooms including bedrooms, stairways, and bathrooms.

## 3.4 Controls for ancillary works


### 3.4.1 Car parking and vehicular access

Except for the number of car parking spaces, this plan adopts the other requirements for car parking and vehicle access in the Housing Code (Codes SEPP, Part 3).

Any variation to these controls must meet these performance criteria. Garages and carports should:

Under Part F (Transport and Parking Management) of this plan , a new driveway crossing may be required if the proposal involves a change to the vehicle access arrangements and/or car parking spaces.

Also see Part F for more information on car parking and vehicular access.

3.4.2 Earthworks, retaining walls, drainage, protection of walls, and protection of trees

This plan adopts the requirements of the Housing Code (Codes SEPP, Part 3) for earthworks, retaining walls, drainage, protection of walls, and protection of trees.

Any variation of these controls must show that any excavation, fill or construction of retaining walls or any works in proximity to trees, due to a variation of the development controls, will not have any significant impacts on adjoining and nearby residential properties or the health of the trees retained on the site.

### 3.4.4 Swimming pools

This plan adopts the requirements of the Housing Code (Codes SEPP, Part 3) for the construction or installation of a swimming pool and/or spa.

Any variation of these controls must show that the swimming pool, due to the variation of the development control, will not have any significant impacts on adjoining and nearby residential properties.


# 4 Major developments

Major development is where the development consists of:

This includes for boarding houses that exceed 300m 2 or 12 persons, manor houses, multi dwelling housing, attached dwellings, residential flat buildings, seniors housing, 'build-to-rent' housing, and the residential component of shop top housing and mixed use developments.

'Multi dwelling housing' is often referred to as townhouses, and 'attached dwellings' are often described as terraces or semi-detached dwellings.

Apartments in a 'shop top housing' development must be above the ground floor level comprising retail or business premises. 'Mixed use' developments comprise two or more different land uses, one of which can include residential apartments.

## 4.1 Strategies and plans

Willoughby City Council has prepared several studies and strategies to set the direction for commercial and residential development in key locations in the local area.

Part L of this plan sets out specific performance criteria and controls for local centres. These include performance criteria and controls for residential flat buildings and the residential components of shop top housing and mixed used developments.

A brief description of the strategies adopted to inform these place-based plans is below.


### 4.1.1 Willoughby Local Centres Strategy 2036

The strategy aims to revitalise the local economy and provides the framework for future planning controls to achieve thriving, attractive and distinctive local centres.

Those centres are:

The Artarmon local centre is on Hampden Road and Wilkes Plaza, adjacent to the Artarmon railway station. The place based plan includes development opportunities for residential accommodation in shop top housing developments. Performance criteria and controls are included to maintain the fine grain shopfronts and retain the heritage values of the Artarmon Heritage Conservation Area.

The Castlecrag local centre is on Edinburgh Road between Eastern Valley Way and Rutland Avenue/The Postern. The place based plan includes development opportunities for residential accommodation in shop top housing developments, and residential flat buildings at 95-103 Edinburgh Road. Any future development must respect the heritage values of the Griffin Heritage Conservation Area.

![page 17 img 1 (189x36)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0017-4c2e542d2bf5.png)
![page 17 img 2 (34x36)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0008-9ff31242d9ed.png)

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part B: Residential Development 2023

The North Willoughby local centre is around the intersection of Penshurst Street and Victoria Avenue, extending south to Patrick Street. The place based plan includes development opportunities for residential accommodation in shop top housing developments.

The High Street local centre is on the eastern side of High Street, bounded by McClelland Street and Glover Street. The place based plan includes development opportunities for residential accommodation in shop top housing developments. Performance criteria and controls are included for upper level setbacks at the rear to protect the residential amenity of adjoining dwellings.

The Naremburn local centre is on the western side of Willoughby Road, bounded by Quiamong Street, Bongalong Street and Glenmore Street. The centre includes two heritage items. The place based plan includes development opportunities for residential accommodation in shop top housing developments. However, any future development must maintain the fine grain shopfronts, and respect the heritage values of the heritage items at 284/284A and 272-276 Willoughby Road.

The commercial precinct of Northbridge is along the major arterial roads of Sailors Bay Road, Eastern Valley Way and Strathallen Avenue. Northbridge Plaza is on the north-eastern corner of Eastern Valley Way and Sailors Bay Road. The place based plan includes development opportunities for residential accommodation within shop top housing developments, and residential flat buildings on the southern side of Sailors Bay Road and at the rear of the Northbridge Plaza.

The Penshurst Street commercial centre is located along, and north of Mowbray Road. There is an eclectic mix of business premises, shop top housing, and a small retail shopping strip on the eastern side of Penshurst Street near Oakville Road. The place based plan includes development opportunities for residential accommodation within shop top housing developments. Performance criteria and controls are included for upper level setbacks at the rear to protect the residential amenity of adjoining dwellings.

The commercial area of the Willoughby South local centre predominantly fronts Willoughby Road with additional commercial areas branching off Frenchs Road. The place based plan includes development opportunities for residential accommodation within shop top housing developments, and residential flat buildings.

See the full strategy for more information and the vision for each local centre at willoughby.nsw.gov.au.

## 4.2 Controls for medium and high density residential development

The relevant controls of the plans, policies and guidelines below apply to medium and high density residential development. This ensures a consistent approach when assessing development applications.

4.2.1 State Environmental Planning Policy (Exempt and Complying Development Codes) 2008

The statutory controls for height of building, floor space ratio and minimum lot size in Willoughby LEP apply to manor houses, attached dwellings and multi dwelling housing.

This plan also adopts many of the controls under Part 3B of the Low Rise Housing Diversity Code (Codes SEPP) for these types of development in the R3 zone. A notable exception is the landscaped area controls.

Any development for manor houses, attached dwellings and multi dwelling housing should satisfy the objectives and design criteria under Low Rise Housing Diversity Design Guide, Department of Planning Industry and Environment, July 2020. The guide is at State Environmental Planning Policy (Exempt and Complying Development Codes) 2008.

Notes:

- The term 'manor houses' is defined in Section 1.5 of the Codes SEPP.
- The terms 'attached dwellings' and 'multi dwelling housing' are defined in Willoughby LEP.
- If there is any inconsistency between the Low Rise Housing Diversity Design Guide and the performance criteria and controls in this part or any other parts of this plan, the provisions in this plan prevail.

### 4.2.2 State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021

The Housing SEPP provides design principles and planning controls that set aside any local planning controls that would prevent the development of housing for seniors or people with a disability that meets the development criteria and standards of this policy.

Note:

- The provisions and controls of the Housing SEPP apply to any proposed seniors housing development in the R2 and C4 zones.
The Housing SEPP is at State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021 - NSW Legislation.

4.2.3 State Environmental Planning Policy No 65 - Design Quality of Residential Apartment Development

The Apartment Design SEPP applies to residential apartments if the building is 3 or more storeys and contains 4 or more dwellings.

The Apartment Design SEPP is at legislation.nsw.gov.au.


### 4.2.4 Apartment Design Guide, NSW Department of Planning and Environment, July 2015

The Apartment Design Guide provides design criteria and general guidance on how development proposals can achieve the design quality principles in the Apartment Design SEPP.

If there is any inconsistency between this plan and the Apartment Design Guide, the requirements, standards and controls in the guide prevail.

The guide is at planning.nsw.gov.au/apartmentdesignguide.

Notes:

- Clause 50 of Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulations 2000 requires an application that relates to a development for residential apartments to include a 'design verification statement' prepared by a qualified designer.
- The statement must show how the proposal achieves the design quality principles under SEPP 65 and how it addresses the objectives in Parts 3 and 4 of the Apartment Design Guide.
- The Apartment Design Guide applies to the residential component of a shop top housing or mixed use development in all zones where such land uses are permissible.

### 4.3.2 Street frontage

The minimum street frontage is 27m. This is to ensure vehicles can enter and leave a site in a forward direction, and adequate landscaped areas are provided along the streetscape.


### 4.3.3 Adaptable housing, access, and mobility

Adaptable housing is governed by Australian Standard AS 4299-1995 Adaptable Housing. Adaptable housing must be provided to accommodate people with mobility impairment, including access and facilities for people in a wheelchair.

A minimum number of adaptable dwellings must be provided for all manor houses, attached dwellings, multi dwelling housing, residential flat buildings, and the residential components of shop top housing and mixed use developments. The number of dwellings must be rounded up if there is 0.5 or more of a dwelling. The minimum numbers are:

Under AS 4299, a dwelling is classified as Class A, B or C, depending on the number of features specified. AS 4299 designates features as 'essential', 'first priority desirable' or 'desirable'.

Class A includes all essential and desirable features. Class B has all essential and at least 50% of desirable features, including those designated as 'first priority'. Class C has all essential features incorporated in the design.

Willoughby City Council requires adaptable dwellings to be designed and constructed to a Class C standard; however, Class A and B are encouraged.

The architectural plans must identify which apartments/dwellings are designed as adaptable.

The communal areas of a proposed development must provide a 'continuous accessible path of travel' to assist people with disability to access facilities independently, equitably and with dignity. The development should include ramps and toilets for people who use a wheelchair; appropriate lighting and colour contrast for people with a visual impairment; tactile surface indicators for people who are blind; and any other appropriate measures to assist people with a disability.

Details are required to be submitted with the development application to demonstrate the proposal will comply with the Disability (Access to Premises - Building) Standards 2010 under the Disability Discrimination Act 1992 .


### 4.3.4 Energy efficiency

Willoughby City Council encourages applying best practice principles in the design and construction of buildings to create energy efficient and environmentally sustainable buildings.

All major developments are required to comply with the relevant provisions of Part J (Building Sustainability) of this plan.


### 4.3.5 Bicycle and car parking

Willoughby City Council encourages alternative and sustainable transport strategies to reduce the reliance on motor vehicles as the principal mode of transport. All developments with 20 dwellings/apartments or more must submit a travel demand management plan.

More information on traffic and parking matters is in Part F (Transport and Parking Management) of this plan.


### 4.3.6 Water management and conservation

All major developments must provide onsite detention systems to capture and detain stormwater runoff for recycling (including irrigation systems for landscaped areas), and to mitigate the impacts of flooding.

The development application must include details of stormwater management. See Part I (Stormwater Management) of this plan for more information.


### 4.3.7 Urban heat

Willoughby City Council encourages applying 'best practice' principles in the design and construction of buildings and other measures to reduce the impacts of urban heat island effects.

This means increasing landscaped areas and the number of trees with large canopies, reducing hard surfaces, encouraging alternative and active transport, and applying water management, including water sensitive urban design principles.

Buildings should also use external materials, façade elements and glazing to limit solar reflectivity to minimise urban heat impacts. This may include retractable shade structures, 'green' walls and roofs, and/or rooftop solar panels.

Roofs should achieve these Solar Reflectance Index (SRI) values:

### 4.3.8 Waste management

Willoughby City Council has adopted the Waste Management Technical Guide and Development Controls by North Sydney Regional Organisation of Councils for multi dwelling housing, residential flat buildings and mixed-use developments.

The technical guide provides comprehensive information to achieve best practice design and construction of waste management and recycling systems.

The development controls provide specific requirements for internal waste storage facilities, individual bin storage areas, communal bin storage areas, bin carting routes, and access for collection vehicles.

All major residential developments must comply with the technical guide and the specific controls for multi dwelling housing, residential flat buildings, and mixed-use buildings.

A copy of Waste Management Technical Guide and Development Controls is at willoughby.nsw.gov.au.


### 4.3.9 Safety by design

All major developments are required to include safety and security measures to prevent criminal activity. Crime prevention measures include high visibility to front entries, careful siting of shrubs and landscape elements, and lighting of pathways or hidden spaces.

The development application must include details of the design and safety measures incorporated into the design.

All services, including overhead electricity wires, are to be located underground for major development. This includes publicly owned land immediately outside the development site.

Section 2C of the Apartment Design Guide details matters to consider when setting the height of buildings. # 5 Controls for other residential land uses


## 5.1 Secondary dwellings

A secondary dwelling may be built as complying development subject to certain standards under the Housing SEPP.

A development application is required if any part of the proposal does not satisfy the criteria under the SEPP. The application will be assessed in line with the performance criteria and relevant controls in this part of Willoughby DCP.


## 5.2 Bed and breakfast accommodation

Bed and breakfast accommodation is complying development under Part 4A (General Development Code) of Codes SEPP, except on bush fire prone land, and subject to certain development standards.

A development application is required if a proposed bed and breakfast accommodation development does not fully satisfy all the criteria under the code. The proposal will be assessed on its individual merits, with particular regard to any likely impacts on the residential amenity of adjoining and nearby residents.

Note:

## 5.3 Boarding houses

Under the Housing SEPP, boarding houses that provide 'affordable housing' in an 'accessible area' may be carried out with consent, subject to compliance with certain development standards.

If a proposal for this type of development is not lodged under the Housing SEPP, applications will be assessed against the standards in the Housing SEPP, and the relevant performance criteria and controls in this plan.

A plan of management must be submitted with an application for a boarding house. It must include details on the topics below to ensure the premises is maintained and operates effectively without impacting on adjoining and nearby residents:

Notes:

- A copy of the plan of management must be provided to all residents and displayed in a prominent location in the premises at all times.
- The plan of management must contain provisions to ensure compliance with the Boarding Houses Act 2012 and the Boarding Houses Regulations 2013 .
- A boarding house is required to be maintained and operated in a single entity. Subdivision is not permitted.

## 5.4 Build-to-rent housing

Build-to-rent housing is permissible with consent under the Housing SEPP. Any application for this type of development will be assessed in line with the performance criteria and any relevant controls under this part of Willoughby DCP and the Apartment Design Guide.

Note:

- If the identified development standards under the Housing SEPP are complied with, Willoughby City Council cannot apply more onerous standards.

## 7.1 18-26 Eric Road and 487-503 Pacific Highway, Artarmon

![page 29 img 1 (624x447)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0029-04b1be61dd05.png)


*Map 1 18-26 Eric Road and 487-503 Pacific Highway, Artarmon*


### 7.1.1 Rear setback

All new developments must provide a minimum rear setback of 12m. This is to provide adequate separation and landscaped area and minimise the impact on privacy and solar access to adjacent properties.


#### 7.2 33-35 Garland Road, Naremburn


### 7.2.1 Pedestrian access

To achieve a 3m wide pedestrian pathway to Hallstrom Park, any new development must dedicate a 1.5m wide strip of land on the western side of 33 Garland Road and the eastern side of 35 Garland Road.

Note:

- For the purposes of calculating the floor space ratio, the total floor area can include the area of land dedicated as public open space.

<!-- SRC: 01-part-b-residential-development.pdf | PAGE: 30 -->

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part B: Residential Development 2023


## 7.3 Crowley Lane, Naremburn


### 7.3.1 Deed of Agreement

New developments bordering Crowley Lane between Nolan Crescent and Park Road must enter into a deed of agreement to purchase and consolidate half the width of the laneway for the full width of the development site.


#### 7.4 1-7 Hotham Street and 2 Wyvern Avenue, Chatswood

![page 30 img 1 (362x439)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0030-508349f7c65c.png)


*Map 2 1-7 Hotham Street and 2 Wyvern Avenue, Chatswood*


### 7.4.1 Vehicular access

All vehicle access is to be provided from Hotham Street. This is to ensure safe egress by diverting vehicle access away from the intersection of Wyvern Avenue and the Pacific Highway.


### 7.4.2 Drainage/flooding

Any new development must submit a flood study to identify the existing flood extent and show the development will not adversely affect any adjoining properties. No structures other than suspended/elevated vehicular crossings are permitted over the identified flood extent.

- Any future development of the site must dedicate a drainage easement in favour of, and at no cost to, Willoughby City Council.

#### Willoughby Development Control Plan Part B: Residential Development 2023


#### Objectives

The allotment size and consolidation objectives are to ensure:

- the allotments are amalgamated to ensure the site area can achieve the stated development potential, provide adequate space for landscaping, and avoid isolating any allotments subject to this section of Willoughby DCP from future development
- the site is amalgamated to enable the substantial redevelopment of the site for high density residential development
- the development is complementary to the scale and character of development in the area
- high quality, built form outcomes and design excellence is encouraged

#### Controls


#### Objectives

The setback and streetscape objectives are to ensure:

- future development appropriately recognises the streetscape and contributes to the public domain
- residential development proposed on the site is consistent with the design criteria in the Apartment Design Guide

#### Controls

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part B: Residential Development 2023

- Structural root zone SRZ defines the area required for tree stability and is required when encroachment into the TPZ is proposed. It is nominally circular with the tree trunk at its centre, expressed by the radius measured from the centre of the trunk. See AS 4970: 2009 section 3.3.5.
- Trunk diameter at breast height DBH is the nominal trunk diameter at 1.4m above ground level
- Tree protection zone TPZ is the area above and below ground to protect the tree crown and roots. The tree protection zone radius is calculated by TPZ=12×DBH, minimum 2m.

#### Objectives

The objectives for access, parking and transport are to:

- ensure the development meets Willoughby City Council's car parking requirements for sites on major public transport corridors
- minimise the number of vehicle access points
- mitigate traffic generated from the proposed development
- ensure the design of vehicle access points minimises the impact on pedestrians and the flow of traffic
- ensure vehicle access points are unobtrusive in the streetscape but visible for motorists and approaching pedestrians

#### Controls


#### Objectives

The objectives for environmental considerations are to ensure:

- the design of the new development minimises the overshadowing impact on adjoining development
- the shape, location and height of buildings are designed to satisfy wind criteria for public safety and comfort at ground level

*Figure 10 Indicative Building Envelope Section*


#### Objectives

- To achieve an appropriate height transition across the site responding to the existing and future desired context; and
- To provide various height controls that maintain sunlight access into nearby residential development and enhance solar access through the site.

#### Controls

- The maximum height of buildings is 18 metres in accordance with the Willoughby Local Environmental Plan 2012. The height of buildings in storeys are to be in accordance with the Figure 1 - Building Envelope Plan .
- The form of the development on the site is to be positioned to reduce solar impacts on the public domain and neighbouring residential properties and provide a transition in scale to The Great Northern Hotel heritage item.

#### Objectives

- To encourage innovative, high quality architectural design; and
- To achieve long term durability of design and finish.

#### Controls

- Before granting development consent for the erection of a new building development, the Council must consider the quality of the architectural design and the achievement of design excellence.
- In considering the quality of the architectural design, the Council must consider feedback received from a Design Review Panel for developments up to 35m high.
- Achievement of design excellence will include achievement of higher building sustainability standards.
![page 49 img 2 (34x36)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0008-9ff31242d9ed.png)

#### Willoughby Development Control Plan Part B: Residential Development 2023

- Any amelioration measurers for environmental impacts such as architectural elements and landscaping are integrated into the design to achieve an overall high standard of design quality.
- Demonstration of adaptive reuse of the Heritage Items 8-10 Moriarty Road is to be shown in accordance with Council requirements as part of any development application.

#### Objectives

- To ensure future development recognises the existing streetscape and contributes to the public domain; and
- To ensure residential development proposed on the site is consistent with the design criteria contained within the Apartment Design Guide.

#### Controls

- Minimum building setbacks from boundaries are to be in accordance with Figure 9.
- Design of the development is not to read as a single mass when viewed from Bowen Street.
- The design of the development is to incorporate a visually interesting façade through the use of articulation, modulation and materials.
- New building envelopes proposed behind the existing heritage items at 8-10 Moriarty Road must not exceed 3 storeys, and must not be positioned less than 1m from the principal building form of the heritage terrace, or not less than a 9m setback from Moriarty Road.

#### Objectives

- Retain and protect existing significant trees in the public domain;
- Landscaping is to soften and complement the development; and
- Landscaping at street level shall improve the amenity and appearance of the pedestrian environment and public domain.

#### Controls

- The planting to the setback areas is to maintain clear sight lines between the entrances and the street and within the planted areas.
- Open space within front setback areas are to present useable and accessible open space that improves the public domain.
- Additional street tree planting will be required for new development. The location and species of new planting will be nominated by Council as part of any development consent.
- Landscaped areas are to be adequately irrigated and drained.
- The redevelopment of the site is to provide the inclusion of soft landscaping.
- Variation to the maximum site coverage and recreational open space requirements within Part D2 of the Willoughby DCP 2006 can be considered provided communal open space proposed

#### Objectives

- The number of vehicle access points to the development are minimised;

#### Willoughby Development Control Plan Part B: Residential Development 2023

- Traffic generated from the proposed development should be mitigated;
- Vehicular access points are designed to minimise their impact on pedestrians and the flow of traffic; and
- Vehicular access points should be unobtrusive in the streetscape but ensure visibility for motorists and approaching pedestrians.

#### Controls

- Proposed vehicular access points are to be limited to no more than one ingress/egress per street frontage.
- Future development of the site must ensure that measures are put in place so that development will have no significant impact on the efficiency and operation of the existing surrounding road network.
- Active transport facilities including resident and visitor bicycle parking are to be provided.
- Bicycle access/facilities and circulation along Bowen Street and Moriarty Road shall be encouraged, particularly in relation to providing future connectivity to the Pacific Highway, including 'filling the gaps' in the existing bicycle network across intersections.
- Electric car charge points are to be provided within any basement car park.
- Car parking rates are to be in accordance with Council requirements, or requirements for a site within a railway precinct and major public transport corridor, or to standards in the RMS Guide to Traffic Generating Development, whichever is the lesser.
- Provide a cul-de-sac at the end of Bowen Street to facilitate vehicle turning movements through Council reservation of a strip of land at 23-29 Bowen Street as shown below in Figure 13.

#### Objectives

- The design of new development shall minimise the overshadowing impact on adjoining development;
- The shape, location and height of buildings should be designed to satisfy wind criteria for public safety and comfort at ground level;

#### Controls

- Any wind amelioration measures shall be integrated into the overall architectural or landscape design of a site.
- Development is encouraged to exceed the minimum requirements of State Environmental Planning Policy (Building Sustainability Index: BASIX) 2004 .
- A minimum GBCA 5-star green star rating for residential flat buildings is required for any proposed development for residential flat buildings.

#### Willoughby Development Control Plan Part B: Residential Development 2023


#### Objectives

- Allotments should be amalgamated to ensure that sufficient site area is available to achieve the stated development potential, adequate provision for landscaping, and to avoid isolating any allotments subject to this section of the DCP from future redevelopment; and
- Development on any residual allotment can be satisfactorily achieved by having regard to efficient solar access design.

#### Controls

- New development on the site will be required to consolidate all affected allotments.
- A development application for the substantial redevelopment of fewer than all the allotments the subject of this section of the DCP, must be accompanied by evidence that consolidation of all allotments has been reasonably attempted.

#### Objectives

- To ensure the heritage listed terrace pair at 8-10 Moriarty Road is sympathetically incorporated in the redevelopment, and the heritage significance of the terrace pair is retained.
- To mitigate impacts of the proposed development to proximate heritage items including the Great Northern Hotel at 522 Pacific Highway.

#### Controls

- New building additions to the south of the existing heritage listed terrace pair at 8-10 Moriarty Road are to be generally consistent with the built form illustrated within the Building Envelope Plan .
- A development application for the redevelopment of the site is to include consideration to further modulation/ articulation of new development in response to the siting of the heritage item.
- Detailed design of proposal to specifically respond to the bulk, materiality and street wall height of the heritage item.
- The redevelopment of the site is to retain the heritage values of the Local Heritage Items at 8-10 Moriarty Road.

#### Attachment 1: Controls for development in the R2 zone

Except for the floor space ratio (FSR) development standard and the landscaping controls, this component of Willoughby DCP largely aligns with Codes SEPP Part 3 (Housing Code), 3B (Low Rise Housing Diversity Code) as it applies to dual occupancies, and Part 4 (Housing Alterations Code).

If a proposed development has an estimated cost of $50,000 or more, a suitably qualified person must certify it complies with all relevant provisions in Willoughby LEP and the numerical controls in this part of Willoughby DCP.


#### The table comprises:

- Development standards under Willoughby LEP.
- General controls for dwellings, dual occupancies and attached development.
- Amenity development standards.
- Further development controls for detached development.
- Further development controls for detached studios.
- Development controls for swimming pools.
- Development controls for fences.
- Development controls for associated works (earthworks, retaining walls, drainage, protection of walls, and protection of trees).
- Further controls for dual occupancies.
- Further controls for attached dual occupancies where part of one dwelling is located above part of another dwelling.

#### Note :

- The definition of a 'suitably qualified person' includes a practising registered architect, a practising qualified and accredited building designer, a registered building surveyor and a certified practicing planner (CPP).

| <200m 2             |            | 0.65:1    |       |      |       |
| ≥200m 2 and <300m 2 |            | 0.55:1    |       |      |       |
| ≥300m 2 and <400m 2 |            | 0.50:1    |       |      |       |

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part B: Residential Development 2023

Attachment 2: Controls for manor houses, attached dwellings and multi dwelling housing in the R3 zone

The manor house controls for this component of Willoughby DCP generally aligns to Part 3B (Low Rise Housing Diversity Code) of Codes SEPP.

Many of the other controls under the Low Rise Housing Diversity Code are adopted for attached dwellings and multi dwelling housing. Notable exceptions are the landscaped area and setback controls.

A suitably qualified person must certify the proposed development complies with all relevant provisions of Willoughby LEP and the numerical controls under this part of Willoughby DCP. The table comprises:

- Development standards under Willoughby LEP.
- Amenity development standards.
- Controls for manor houses.
- Controls for attached dwellings and multi dwelling housing.
- Controls for detached development.
- Controls for detached studios.

#### Notes:

- A suitably qualified person includes a practicing registered architect, a practicing qualified and accredited building designer, a registered building surveyor and a certified practicing planner (CPP).
- If the proposed development includes construction of a swimming pools, fence, or associated works (earthworks, retaining walls, drainage, protection of walls, and protection of trees), please complete the relevant Sections f, g and h in Attachment 1.
- A concept subdivision layout must be submitted with the application.
- Unless otherwise stated the site area refers to the 'parent lot' which is the entire site area prior to subdivision.
- Further controls apply to individual lots that may be created by subdivision for each dwelling.
- A manor house, attached dwellings or multi dwelling housing must be consistent with the relevant design criteria in the Low Rise Housing Diversity Design Guide, Department of Planning Industry and Environment, July 2020. The requirements of Part B and any other parts of Willoughby DCP and this compliance checklist prevail to the extent of any inconsistency with the design guide.

Attachment 3: Controls for residential flat buildings and the residential components of shop top housing and mixed use developments in the R3 and R4 zones.

This component of Willoughby DCP aligns to the Apartment Design Guide, NSW Department of Planning and Environment, July 2015. It applies to residential flat buildings and the residential components of shop top housing and mixed use developments.

New single dwellings and dual occupancies in the R3 Medium Density zone and R4 High Density zone in the Willoughby LEP 2012 are prohibited. Where alterations and additions are proposed to existing single dwellings in the R3 and R4 zones, the R2 Low Density Residential zone DCP controls would apply (refer Part B Attachment 1).

A practicing registered architect must certify the proposed development complies with all relevant provisions of the Apartment Design Guide, Willoughby LEP and the numerical controls under this part.
