# 13 Controls for specific sites

This section provides controls for any future development for specific sites and areas, and the site specific DCPs that support approved planning proposals in the Chatswood CBD and the Local Centres.


## 13.1 Chatswood CBD

The following specific sites and areas, and the site specific DCPs apply to the Chatswood CBD.


### 13.1.1 767 Pacific Highway, Chatswood

The existing façade of the heritage listed Chatswood Fire Station is to be incorporated within any future development on the site if it is required to be demolished for road widening.


### 13.1.2 61A Albert Avenue Chatswood (Mandarin Centre)


#### 13.1.3.1 General

The controls contained in this site specific Development Control Plan apply to 65 Albert Avenue Chatswood. This land is bounded by Albert Avenue, Victor Street and Orchard Road as shown in Figure 18 below.


<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 48 -->

![page 48 img 1 (602x319)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0048-dcd7dbb44210.png)


*Figure 18: Site Aerial Map*


# 1 Objectives of the Plan

The Objectives of the Plan are to:

- Support the provision of non-residential development in the Chatswood CBD.
- Enable the development of the site without impacting the viability of adjoining land.
- Provide a building exhibiting design excellence in architectural form and materials.
- Minimise traffic impacts on the surrounding road network.
- Maximise street level activation.
- Built Form

## Performance Criteria

The built form of new development shall:

- Achieve a slender tower/s on the site.
- Achieve a site layout that provides a pleasant environment for the occupants and minimises impact on surrounding properties and streetscape.
- Ensure visual and acoustic privacy and sun access.
- Provide suitable areas for communal open spaces, deep soil zones and landscaping.
- Minimise view loss for surrounding properties.

## Controls

- The width of each side of any tower, and design elements that contribute to building bulk, are to be minimised.
- If there is more than one tower on a site, sufficient separation is to be provided in accordance with required setbacks to ensure slender tower forms are achieved.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 49 -->

- Two towers must not visually read as one large tower. Towers are not to be linked above Podium and should operate independently regarding lifts and services.
- The site layout, including any tower/s within the site, is to be in accordance with Figure 19.
![page 49 img 1 (532x385)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0049-7c938d2e8e0d.png)


*Figure 19: Site Layout*


## 3.0 Height of Building


### Performance Criteria

The height of the new development shall:

- Be consistent with the permitted Height of Buildings development standard applicable to the site.
- Minimise overshadowing of surrounding properties and the nearby key public spaces and public domain.

### Controls

- The maximum building height is to include all structures located at roof level, including lift over runs and any other architectural features.
- All roof top lift over runs or exposed structures are to be integrated with the building.
- Flat roof areas shall incorporate useable outdoor recreation space where suitable.

## 4.0 Setbacks and street frontage heights


<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 50 -->


### Performance Criteria

Setbacks shall:

- Ensure the positioning of new buildings are consistent with the proposed streetscape envisioned for Chatswood CBD and contained in the Chatswood CBD Planning and Urban Design Strategy 2036.
- Be provided at ground level to contribute to public realm.
- Contribute to slender tower forms.
- Minimise the effects of adverse wind conditions at street level.
Street wall heights shall:

- Ensure the street wall heights are consistent with the street wall heights envisioned for Chatswood CBD and contained in the Chatswood CBD Planning and Urban Design Strategy 2036.

### Controls

The development is to have a maximum street wall height of 24m at any point.

- Minimum 6 metre setback above street wall to tower.
- Victor Street
- Maximum 24 metre street wall height at front boundary.
- Minimum 6 metre setback above street wall to tower.

### Performance Criteria

### Performance Criteria

- Greening at the podium roof level is to be provided, with planting visible to the surrounding area - with particular regard to Albert Avenue and Victor Street.
- Podium and roof tops are to be a combination of green and recreation spaces.
- Street tree planting is to be provided.

- Public domain improvements shall be provided to all street frontages to Council requirement
- A minimum of 20% of the site is to be provided as soft landscaping, which may be located on ground, podium and roof top levels or green walls of buildings.

Ausgrid lighting poles are to be provided to the requirements of Ausgrid for street lighting and shall be positioned compatible to the landscaping design around the site.

## 9.0 Active Street Frontages


### Performance Criteria

- To ensure that uses on the ground level contribute to the activation of the public domain.
- To ensure that design and location of ground floor uses maximise surveillance of the public domain.

### Controls

- At ground level buildings are to maximise active frontages to Albert Avenue and Victor Street.

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part L: Place Based Plans 2023

- A building has an active street frontage if all premises on the ground floor of the building facing the street(s) are used for the purpose of commercial premises or non-residential purposes and provide elements of visual interest when viewed from the street.

## 10.0 Traffic and Transport


### Performance Criteria

- Development must be designed to provide adequate and safe access to the site.
- Development on the site is not the cause of adverse traffic impacts on the surrounding road system.
- Minimise the number of vehicular access points to the development.
- All vehicles are to enter and exit the site in a forward direction.
- Traffic and transport solutions are to be physical (rather than mechanical) on this site.
- Minimise car parking and encourage alternative transport options.

### Controls

- Vehicle access to the development is to be from one access point in Victor Street.
- Vehicle egress from the development is to be from one access point in Orchard Road.
- Vehicle access and egress is to be designed and located to achieve safety, minimise conflicts between pedestrians and vehicles and create a high quality streetscape.
- All car parking and loading facilities are to be located below ground level.
- Other strategies for car parking reduction, such as reciprocal arrangements for sharing parking and car share, is to be included in any future Development Application.

## 11.0 Waste Management, Loading and Services


### Performance Criteria

- All loading, unloading and servicing is required to occur on-site.
- To ensure that adequate provision is made for waste storage and disposal.
- Floor space at ground level is to be maximised.

### Controls

- All loading and unloading services are required to occur at basement level on-site.
- Other supporting functions such as garbage rooms, plant and other services are to be located in basement levels.
- A Waste Management Plan shall be submitted at the Development Application stage.
- Substations are to be provided within buildings, not within the streets, open spaces or setbacks and not facing key active street frontages.

- Achievement of design excellence shall include achievement of higher building sustainability standards.

### Controls

## 15.0 Amusement Centres


### General

- These special controls apply to the development of amusement centres within the Mandarin Centre, Chatswood. All applications for amusement centres require development consent from the Council. When development applications for amusement centres are being assessed, local schools, Police and Council's Community Services Division will be consulted.

### Objectives

- Accommodate the establishment of a quality amusement centre within the Mandarin Centre;
- Ensure that the operation of the amusement centre does not cause problems for schools within the area;
- Ensure that the amusement centre is a functional and well supervised facility;
- Achieve an open, pleasant and safe environment for all those wishing to play amusement devices; and
- Ensure that the use does not cause any form of nuisance or social disturbance.

### Location

- Amusement centres must only be located within the managed centre.
- Amusement centres shall not be located at natural ground level if the premises has direct access to a street, lane, mall or public place.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 56 -->

- The entrance to the amusement centre shall not be located within 20m of the entrance of the managed centre.

### Additional Considerations

- In respect of any development application for an amusement centre, Council will take into consideration the following matters:
- any representations made by a statutory body or other interested persons in relation to the application;
- the necessity and desirability of making provision on site for the parking of cars and bicycles;
- the existing and future amenity of the neighbourhood;
- whether the proposed development is likely to cause a nuisance due to the emission of noise, vibration, congregations in public places, or otherwise adversely affect the environment;
- the social effect of the use in the locality and the public interest;
- access for people with disabilities; and
- the location of premises in relation to residential areas and schools.

### Operational Requirements

- Hours of operation
- Amusement centres shall not operate outside the approved hours of the Mandarin Centre.
- Building Code of Australia
- Buildings will be required to comply with the requirements of the Building Code of Australia for a class 9(b) building and a 'place of public entertainment'. The number of persons on the premises at any one time shall be limited to one (1) person per 1.2m 2 of gross floor area.
- Management of Patrons
- No person who is in effective control of an amusement centre shall permit to enter or remain thereon any person under the age of eighteen (18) years except:
- at an hour or on a day when primary or secondary schools are not open; or
- where the person submits satisfactory evidence to those in management that they are either not enrolled as a student at a primary or secondary school, or absent from school with the approval of the school.
- An amusement centre shall be attended during all hours of operation by at least one person, or if Council so decides depending on the size of the facility, two or more persons, and any such person(s) shall be recognisable as an attendant. The attendant(s) is to be responsible for the effective control of the centre and to ensure that the conditions of any consent applying to the centre are complied with so as to achieve the objectives of Part E3.3.3 of this plan.
- No alcohol or drugs are to be permitted on the premises at any time.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 57 -->

- Amusement Devices
- An amusement centre shall not contain any amusement device which is or can be operated for profit or reward by the player(s) where such profit or reward is in the form of money.
- Generation of Crowds
- The operation of the premises is not to adversely affect the amenity of the surrounding area, by allowing people to congregate in a public place.
- An applicant will need to submit details of appropriate management measures to satisfy this requirement.
- Noise Transmission
- Materials of construction shall be such that the noise transmission rating shall achieve a sound level not exceeding 5dB/A above the ambient level of any adjoining building or public place. This does not include other occupancies within the managed centre.

- Other strategies for car parking reduction, such as reciprocal arrangements for sharing parking and car share, are to be included in any future Development Application.

# 11. Waste Management, Loading and Services


## Performance Criteria

- All loading, unloading and servicing is required to occur on-site.
- To ensure that adequate provision is made for waste storage and disposal.
- Floor space at ground level is to be maximised, with services located in basement.

## Controls

- All loading and unloading services are required to occur at basement level on-site.
- Other supporting functions such as garbage rooms, plant and other services are to be located in basement levels.
- A Waste Management Plan shall be submitted at the Development Application stage.
- Substations are to be provided within buildings, not within the streets, open spaces or setbacks and not facing key active street frontages. Substations are to be designed to ensure protection of residents from Electro Magnetic Radiation (EMR) emissions.

# 12. Design Excellence


## Performance Criteria

- Ensure high quality and varied design through the use of competitive design processes.
- Implement a rigorous process to support good design outcomes.

## Controls

- All developments that have a height of 35m or more are subject to a competitive design process.
- The competitive design process must be undertaken in accordance with the Willoughby Design Excellence Policy and Willoughby Design Excellence Guidelines.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 74 -->


# 13. Public Art


## Performance Criteria

- All redevelopments in the Chatswood CBD should contribute to public art in accordance with Council's Public Art Policy.

## Controls

- Public Art is to be provided in accordance with Council's Public Art Policy.

# 14. Building Sustainability


## Performance Criteria

- Design excellence shall include achievement of higher building sustainability standards.

## Controls

- A minimum of 5 stars GBCA building rating is required. A higher rating is encouraged. An assessment report is to be submitted at Development Application stage.

## 13.1.5 753 Pacific Highway and 15 Ellis Street Chatswood


# 1. General

The controls contained in this Site Specific Development Control Plan applies to 753 Pacific Highway and 15 Ellis Street, Chatswood. The land is bounded by Pacific Highway to the west, Ellis Street to the south, Crispe Lane to the east and 755-759 Pacific Highway to the north as shown on Figure 24 below.


<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 75 -->

![page 75 img 1 (928x680)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0075-e120f56bfd43.png)


*Figure 24: Site Aerial Map*


## Objectives of the Plan

The aims and objectives of this Plan are to:

- Provide guidelines for a mixed use development on the site.
- Provide a development that ensures the viability of adjoining and surrounding sites for future development.
- Minimise traffic impacts on the surrounding road network.
- Ensure development on the site minimises impacts to the amenity of neighbouring residential properties.
- Provide landscaping in and surrounding the site that enhances the presentation of the site as well as the amenity of the development.
- Achieves architectural and urban design excellence.

# 2. Built Form


## Performance Criteria

The built form of the new development shall:

- Achieve a slender tower form on the site.
- Achieve a site layout that provides a pleasant environment for the occupants and minimises impact on surrounding properties.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 76 -->

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part L: Place Based Plans 2023

- Ensure visual and acoustic privacy, natural ventilation, sun access, and views.
- Provide suitable areas for communal open spaces, deep soil zones, and landscaping.

## Controls

- The maximum tower floor plate that applies to this site for residential towers above a podium is 700m 2 .
- The width of each side of any tower should be minimised and design elements that contribute to building bulk should be minimised.
- The building layout is to be in accordance with Figure 25.
![page 76 img 1 (824x760)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0076-d6ecee9480f6.png)


*Figure 25: Site Layout*


<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 77 -->


# 3. Height of Building


## Performance Criteria

The built form of new development shall:

- Be consistent with the permitted Height of Buildings development standard applicable to the site.
- Minimise overshadowing of surrounding properties, key public spaces and public domain.

## Controls

- The maximum building height is to include all structures located at roof level, including lift over runs and any other architectural features.
- All roof top lift over runs or exposed structures are to be integrated with the building.
- Flat roof areas shall incorporate useable outdoor recreation space where suitable, within the maximum building height.

# 4. Setbacks and Street Frontage Heights


## Performance Criteria

Setbacks shall:

- Ensure the positioning of new buildings is consistent with the proposed streetscape envisioned for Chatswood CBD and contained in the Chatswood CBD Planning and Urban Design Strategy 2036.
- Be provided at ground level to contribute to public realm.
- Contribute at ground level deep soil areas, landscaping, and open space.
- Contribute to slender tower forms.
- Minimise the effects of adverse wind conditions at street level.
Street wall heights shall:

- Ensure such heights are consistent with the street wall heights envisioned for Chatswood CBD and contained in the Chatswood CBD Planning and Urban Design Strategy 2036.

## Controls

- The building setbacks are to be in accordance with Map 5 (Setbacks and street frontage heights). Setbacks are as follows:
- Pacific Highway (western) Frontage:
- Minimum 4 metre setback at ground level from front boundary.
- ii) Maximum 7 metre street wall height (maximum two storeys).
- iii) Minimum 6 metre setback above street wall.
- Ellis Street and Crispe Lane Frontage:
- 6-14 metre street wall height at front boundary (maximum two to four storeys).
- ii) Minimum 3 metre setback above street wall.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 78 -->

- In regards the tower, a minimum of 1:20 ratio of the setback to building height above the podium (eg. tower to be setback 3 metre above podium for a 60 metre building, 4.5 metre setback for a 90 metre building).
- In addition to Control 1:
- Setbacks may be greater and street wall heights may be lower.
- Additional ground level setbacks are sought that contribute to public realm.
![page 78 img 1 (576x448)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0078-9fa36585180c.png)


*Map 5 : Setbacks and street frontage heights*


# 5. Building Exterior


## Performance Criteria

- Buildings are to demonstrate a high design quality when viewed from the public domain and the surrounding area.
- Facade treatment and design is to be used to break down the mass and bulk of buildings.
- High quality façade materials and finishes are to be used which contribute positively to the built environment and mitigate urban heat.

## Controls

- Facades are to be articulated and should incorporate recesses and projecting elements that do not encroach into required setbacks.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 79 -->

- Extensive blank walls shall be avoided at street level.

# 6. Amenity


## Performance Criteria

- Maximise solar access and ventilation to residential units.
- Ensure visual and acoustic privacy of residential units in the development and adjoining properties.
- Improve pedestrian amenity surrounding the site.

## Controls

- A Wind Assessment shall be submitted at Development Application Stage.
- A detailed Acoustic Assessment shall be submitted at Development Application Stage.
- Residential units shall be designed to maximize solar access, cross ventilation, visual and acoustic privacy.

# 7. Open Space and Landscaping


## Performance Criteria

- Landscaping is to soften and complement the development.
- Landscaping at street level shall improve the amenity and appearance of the pedestrian environment.
- The development shall provide publicly accessible links and open space.
- Publicly accessible open space is to include meaningful green landscaping.
- Greening at the podium roof level is to be provided, with planting visible to the surrounding area - with particular regard to Pacific Highway, Ellis Street, Crispe Lane and neighbouring properties.
- Podium and roof tops are to be a combination of green and recreation spaces.
- Street tree planting is to be provided.

## Controls

- Open space at ground level shall be utilised as publicly accessible open space.
- All roofs up to 30 metres from ground are to be green roofs. These are to provide a balance of passive and active green spaces that maximize solar access.
- A minimum of 2 hours of sun access is to be provided to the public open space on the site.
- Public domain improvements shall be provided to all street frontages to Council requirements.
- A minimum of 20% of the site is to be provided as soft landscaping, which may be located on ground, podium and roof top levels or green walls of buildings.
- Deep soil planting is to be provided within the 4m setback to Pacific Highway. Deep soil plantings include trees and shrubs, and are to be unimpeded by buildings or structures below ground.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 80 -->

- A Landscape Plan is to be provided at Development Application stage detailing all public domain at ground level, street tree planting, planting and space allocation at podium and roof top levels. This is to include species, container size at planting, spacing and approximate size at maturity.
- Street tree planting is at the cost of the proponent, with location and species to be determined in consultation with Council at Development Application stage.
- All existing aerial cables which may include for electricity, communications and other cables connecting to street poles and buildings around the site shall be removed and installed underground in accordance with the requirements of the relevant service authorities. Ausgrid lighting poles are to be provided to the requirements of Ausgrid for street lighting and shall be positioned compatible to the landscaping design around the site.

# 8. Links


## Performance Criteria

- The development shall provide publicly accessible through site links and open space.
- Publicly accessible open space is to include green landscaping.

## Controls

- The development is to incorporate publicly accessible through site links and open space in accordance with Map 4 below.
- Through site links and open space in addition to Map 4 is required on a site by site basis.
- All publicly accessible open space and links are to be the responsibility of the relevant ownership entity, with formal public access to be created over these areas.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 81 -->

![page 81 img 1 (940x760)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0081-865796cce836.png)


*Map 4: Through Site Links and Open Space*


# 9. Active Street Frontages


## Performance Criteria

- To ensure that uses on the ground level contribute to the activation of the public domain.
- To ensure that design and location of ground floor uses maximize surveillance of the public domain.

## Controls

- At ground level buildings are to maximise active frontages to Pacific Highway, Ellis Street and Crispe Lane.
- A building has an active street frontage if all premises on the ground floor of the building facing the street(s) are used for the purpose of commercial premises or non-residential purposes and provide elements of visual interest when viewed from the street.

# 10. Traffic and Transport


## Performance Criteria

- Development must be designed to provide adequate and safe access to the site.
- Development on the site should not cause adverse traffic impacts on the surrounding road system.

- Ensure visual and acoustic privacy of residential units in the development, adjoining properties and properties on the other side of the street.
- Improve pedestrian amenity surrounding the site.

## Controls

- A Wind Assessment shall be submitted at Development Application Stage.
- A detailed Acoustic Assessment shall be submitted at Development Application Stage.
- Residential units shall be designed to maximize solar access, cross ventilation, visual and acoustic privacy.

# 7. Open Space and Landscaping


## Performance Criteria

- Landscaping is to soften and complement the development.
- Landscaping at street level shall improve the amenity and appearance of the pedestrian environment.
- The development shall provide publicly accessible links and open space.
- Publicly accessible open space is to include meaningful green landscaping.
- Greening at the podium roof level is to be provided, with planting visible to the surrounding area - with particular regard to Help Street, McIntosh Street and Cambridge Lane.
- Podium and roof tops are to be a combination of green and recreation spaces.
- Street tree planting is to be provided.

## Controls

- Open space at ground level shall be available as publicly accessible open space.
- Tree planting must be provided along the Cambridge Lane frontage within the 6m setback area (3m being soft landscaping).
- All roofs up to 30 metres from ground are to be green roofs. These are to provide a balance of passive and active green spaces that maximize solar access.
- A minimum of 2 hours of sun access is to be provided to the public open space on the site.
- Public domain improvements shall be provided to all street frontages to Council requirements.
- A minimum of 20% of the site is to be provided as soft landscaping, which may be located on ground, podium and roof top levels or green walls of buildings.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 98 -->

- Deep soil planting is to be provided within the setback to Cambridge Lane. Deep soil plantings include trees and shrubs, and are to be unimpeded by buildings or structures below ground.
- A Landscape Plan is to be provided at Development Application stage detailing all public domain at ground level, street tree planting, planting and space allocation at podium and roof top levels. This is to include species, container size at planting, spacing and approximate size at maturity.
- Street tree planting is at the cost of the proponent, with location and species to be determined in consultation with Council at Development Application stage.
- All existing aerial cables which may include for electricity, communications and other cables connecting to street poles and buildings around the site shall be removed and installed underground in accordance with the requirements of the relevant service authorities. Ausgrid lighting poles are to be provided to the requirements of Ausgrid for street lighting and shall be positioned compatible to the landscaping design around the site.

# 8. Links


## Performance Criteria

- The development shall provide publicly accessible through site links and open space.
- Publicly accessible open space is to include green landscaping.

## Controls

- The development is to incorporate publicly accessible through site links and open space in accordance with Map 4 below.
- Through site links and open space in addition to Map 4 is required on a site by site basis.
- The ground level setback on Help Street, McIntosh Street and Cambridge Lane is to be unobstructed, with the only exception being ground level landscaping.
- All publicly accessible open space and links are to be the responsibility of the relevant ownership entity, with an easement for public access to be created over these areas.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 99 -->

![page 99 img 1 (940x760)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0081-865796cce836.png)


*Map 4: Through Site Links and Open Space*


# 9. Active Street Frontages


## Performance Criteria

- To ensure that uses on the ground level contribute to the activation of the public domain.
- To ensure that design and location of ground floor uses maximize surveillance of the public domain.

## Controls

- At ground level buildings are to maximise active frontages to Help Street, McIntosh Street and Cambridge Lane.
- A building has an active street frontage if all premises on the ground floor of the building facing the street(s) are used for the purpose of commercial premises or non-residential purposes and provide elements of visual interest when viewed from the street.

# 10. Traffic and Transport


## Performance Criteria

- Development must be designed to provide adequate and safe access to the site.
- Development on the site should not cause adverse traffic impacts on the surrounding road system.
- Minimise the number of vehicular access points to the development.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 100 -->

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part L: Place Based Plans 2023

- All vehicles are to enter and exit the site in a forward direction.
- Traffic and transport solutions are to be physical (rather than mechanical) on this site.
- Minimise car parking and encourage alternative transport options.

## Controls

- Vehicle access to / egress from the development is to be minimised.
- Vehicle access and egress is to be designed and located to achieve safety, minimise conflicts between pedestrians and vehicles and create a high quality streetscape.
- All car parking facilities are to be located below ground level.
- Other strategies for car parking reduction, such as reciprocal arrangements for sharing parking and car share, are to be included in any future Development Application.

# 11. Waste Management, Loading and Services


## Performance Criteria

- All loading, unloading and servicing is required to occur on-site.
- Ensure that adequate provision is made for waste storage and disposal.
- Floor space at ground level is to be maximised, with services located in basement.

## Controls

- All loading and unloading services are required to occur at basement level on-site.
- Other supporting functions such as garbage rooms, plant and other services are to be located in basement levels.
- A Waste Management Plan shall be submitted at the Development Application stage.
- Substations are to be provided within buildings, not within the streets, open spaces or setbacks and not facing key active street frontages. Substations are to be designed to ensure protection of residents from Electro Magnetic Radiation (EMR) emissions.

# 12. Design Excellence


## Performance Criteria

- Ensure high quality and varied design through the use of competitive design processes.
- Implement a rigorous process to support good design outcomes.

## Controls

- All developments that have a height of 35m or more are subject to a competitive design process.
- The competitive design process must be undertaken in accordance with the Willoughby Design Excellence Policy and Willoughby Design Excellence Guidelines.

# 13. Public Art


## Performance Criteria

- All redevelopments in the Chatswood CBD should contribute to public art in accordance with Council's Public Art Policy.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 101 -->


## Controls

- Public Art is to be provided in accordance with Council's Public Art Policy.

# 14. Building Sustainability


## Performance Criteria

- Design excellence shall include achievement of higher building sustainability standards.

## Controls

- A minimum of 5 stars GBCA building rating is required. A higher rating is encouraged. An assessment report is to be submitted at Development Application stage.

The controls contained in this Site Specific Development Control Plan applies to 54-56 Anderson Street, Chatswood.

## Objectives of the Plan

The aims and objectives of this Plan are to:

- Provide guidelines for a mixed use development on the site.
- Provide a development that ensures the viability of adjoining and surrounding sites for future development.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 102 -->

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part L: Place Based Plans 2023

- Minimise traffic impacts on the surrounding road network
- Ensure development on the site minimises impacts to the amenity of neighbouring residential properties.
- Provide landscaping in and surrounding the site that enhances the presentation of the site as well as the amenity of the development.
- Achieves architectural and urban design excellence.
- Maximise activation to Anderson Street, O'Brien Street and Wilson Street.

# 2. Built Form


## Performance Criteria

The built form of the new development shall:

- Achieve a slender tower form on the site.
- Achieve a site layout that provides a pleasant environment for the occupants and minimises impact on surrounding properties.
- Ensure visual and acoustic privacy, natural ventilation, sun access, and views.
- Provide suitable areas for communal open spaces, deep soil zones, and landscaping.

## Controls

- The maximum tower floor plate that applies to this site for residential towers above a podium is 700m 2 .
- The width of each side of any tower should be minimised and design elements that contribute to building bulk should be minimised.
- The building layout is to be in accordance with Figure 31.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 103 -->

![page 103 img 1 (904x584)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0103-0ab0b9b88b41.png)


*Figure 31: Site Layout*


# 3. Height of Building


## Performance Criteria

The built form of new development shall:

- Be consistent with the permitted Height of Buildings development standard applicable to the site.
- Minimise overshadowing of surrounding properties, key public spaces and public domain.

## Controls

- The maximum building height is to include all structures located at roof level, including lift over runs and any other architectural features.
- All roof top lift over runs or exposed structures are to be integrated with the building.
- Flat roof areas shall incorporate useable outdoor recreation space where suitable, within the maximum building height.

# 4. Setbacks and Street Frontage Heights


## Performance Criteria

Setbacks shall:

- Ensure the positioning of new buildings is consistent with the proposed streetscape envisioned for Chatswood CBD and contained in the Chatswood CBD Planning and Urban Design Strategy 2036.
- Be provided at ground level to contribute to public realm.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 104 -->

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part L: Place Based Plans 2023

- Contribute at ground level deep soil areas, landscaping, and open space.
- Protect all significant on-site trees and all street trees on Anderson Street, Wilson Street and O'Brien Street.
- Contribute to slender tower forms.
- Minimise the effects of adverse wind conditions at street level.
Street wall heights shall:

- Ensure such heights are consistent with the street wall heights envisioned for Chatswood CBD and contained in the Chatswood CBD Planning and Urban Design Strategy 2036.

## Controls

- The building setbacks are to be in accordance with Map 5 (Setbacks and street frontage heights). Setbacks are as follows:
- Anderson Street frontage
- Minimum 3m setback at ground level
- ii) Minimum 1m setback above street wall
- iii) 6-14 metre street wall height at front boundary (maximum two to four storeys).
- iv) In regards Point d) below, a minimum tower setback above street wall of 4.5m is required from the Anderson Street boundary where height is 90m.
- Wilson Street and O'Brien Street frontage:
- Minimum 3m setback at ground level
- ii) Minimum 3m setback above street wall
- iii) 6-14 metre street wall height at front boundary (maximum two to four storeys).
- North Shore Rail Line boundary
- Minimum 3m setback at ground level
- ii) Minimum 3m setback above street wall
- iii) 6-14 metre street wall height at front boundary (maximum two to four storeys).
- In regards the tower, a minimum of 1:20 ratio of the setback to building height above the podium from all boundaries (eg. tower to be setback a minimum of 2.65 metres above podium for a 53 metre high building, 4.5m for a 90m high building).

- Setbacks may be greater and street wall heights may be lower.
- Additional ground level setbacks are sought that contribute to public realm.

## Controls

- Facades are to be articulated and should incorporate recesses and projecting elements that do not encroach into required setbacks.
- Extensive blank walls shall be avoided at street level.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 109 -->

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part L: Place Based Plans 2023

- All vehicles are to enter and exit the site in a forward direction.
- Traffic and transport solutions are to be physical (rather than mechanical) on this site.
- Minimise car parking and encourage alternative transport options.

## Controls

- Vehicle access to / egress from the development is to be from one access point in O'Brien Street.
- Vehicle access and egress is to be designed and located to achieve safety, minimise conflicts between pedestrians and vehicles and create a high quality streetscape.
- All car parking and loading facilities are to be located below ground level.
- Other strategies for car parking reduction, such as reciprocal arrangements for sharing parking and car share, is to be included in any future Development Application.
- The following is to be provided in any future development application:
- Car parking provision is to be consistent with the requirements of SEPP 65 / constrained parking rates for new developments in the Chatswood CBD as supported by TfNSW.
- A minimum of 1 secure bicycle parking space per apartment.
- A minimum of 1 secure bicycle space per 100m² of non-residential /retail floor space.
- Adequate end of trip facilities including lockers, showers, etc. for use by nonresidential and retail tenants.
- A bicycle rack within the site boundary for use by retail customers.
- A minimum of three (3) freight and service vehicle spaces within the basement, in addition to the one (1) Medium Rigid Vehicle (MRV) space proposed within basement level 1 loading dock.
- Swept path analysis for simultaneous MRV access and egress at the entry to the basement ramp to demonstrate that MRVs can safely pass each other.
- Access arrangements and the operation of basement 1 to be amended to remove conflicts between vehicles accessing and egressing the site.
- Evidence of consultation between the proponent and Sydney Trains, and any conclusions, to ensure that all relevant Sydney Trains matters of consideration are taken into account and are incorporated in the future design of the development.
- Evidence of consultation with TfNSW and service providers in regards any impacts to the bus stop in front of 54 Anderson Street and the no stopping zone on Anderson Street, during construction or in end state.
- A Traffic Management Plan for the construction phase, and future operation phase, to demonstrate that additional vehicular movements in and out of the site do not pose queuing issues along the Wilson Street overbridge, and potentially obstructing rail corridor access.
- Updated traffic analysis and modelling.

## Controls

- All loading and unloading services are required to occur at basement level on-site.
- Other supporting functions such as garbage rooms, plant and other services are to be located in basement levels.
- A Waste Management Plan shall be submitted at the Development Application stage.
- Substations are to be provided within buildings, not within the streets, open spaces or setbacks and not facing key active street frontages. Substations are to be designed to ensure protection of residents from Electro Magnetic Radiation (EMR) emissions.

# 12. Design Excellence


## Performance Criteria

- Ensure high quality and varied design through the use of competitive design processes.
- Implement a rigorous process to support good design outcomes.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 119 -->


## Controls

- All developments that have a height of 35mor more are subject to a competitive design process.
- The competitive design process must be undertaken in accordance with the Willoughby Design Excellence Policy and Willoughby Design Excellence Guidelines.

# 13. Public Art


## Performance Criteria

- All redevelopments in the Chatswood CBD should contribute to public art in accordance with Council's Public Art Policy.

## Controls

- Public Art is to be provided in accordance with Council's Public Art Policy.

# 14. Building Sustainability


## Performance Criteria

- Design excellence shall include achievement of higher building sustainability standards.

## Controls

- A minimum of 5 stars GBCA building rating is required. A higher rating is encouraged. An assessment report is to be submitted at Development Application stage.

## 13.1.10 44-52 Anderson Street Chatswood


# 1. General

The controls contained in this Site Specific Development Control Plan applies to 44-52 Anderson Street, Chatswood.


<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 120 -->

![page 120 img 1 (474x334)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0120-3ee37aed6788.png)


*Figure 34: Site Map*


## Objectives of the Plan

The aims and objectives of this Plan are to:

- Provide guidelines for a mixed use development on the site.
- Provide a development that ensures the viability of adjoining and surrounding sites for future development.
- Minimise traffic impacts on the surrounding road network
- Ensure development on the site minimises impacts to the amenity of neighbouring residential properties.
- Provide landscaping in and surrounding the site that enhances the presentation of the site as well as the amenity of the development.
- Achieves architectural and urban design excellence.
- Maximise activation to Anderson Street, O'Brien Street and Day Street.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 121 -->


# 2. Built Form


## Performance Criteria

The built form of the new development shall:

- Achieve a slender tower form on the site.
- Achieve a site layout that provides a pleasant environment for the occupants and minimises impact on surrounding properties.
- Ensure visual and acoustic privacy, natural ventilation, sun access, and views.
- Provide suitable areas for communal open spaces, deep soil zones, and landscaping.

## Controls

- The maximum tower floor plate that applies to this site for residential towers above a podium is 700m 2 .
- The width of each side of any tower should be minimised and design elements that contribute to building bulk should be minimised.
- The building layout is to be in accordance with Figure 35.
![page 121 img 1 (889x791)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0121-c284ea8d4965.png)


*Figure 35: Site Layout*


<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 122 -->


# 3. Height of Building


## Performance Criteria

The built form of new development shall:

- Be consistent with the permitted Height of Buildings development standard applicable to the site.
- Minimise overshadowing of surrounding properties, key public spaces and public domain.

## Controls

- The maximum building height is to include all structures located at roof level, including lift over runs and any other architectural features.
- All roof top lift over runs or exposed structures are to be integrated with the building.
- Flat roof areas shall incorporate useable outdoor recreation space where suitable, within the maximum building height.

# 4. Setbacks and Street Frontage Heights


## Performance Criteria

Setbacks shall:

- Ensure the positioning of new buildings is consistent with the proposed streetscape envisioned for Chatswood CBD and contained in the Chatswood CBD Planning and Urban Design Strategy 2036.
- Be provided at ground level to contribute to public realm.
- Contribute at ground level deep soil areas, landscaping, and open space.
- Protect all significant on-site trees and all street trees on Anderson Street, O'Brien Street and Day Street.
- Contribute to slender tower forms.
- Minimise the effects of adverse wind conditions at street level.
Street wall heights shall:

- Ensure such heights are consistent with the street wall heights envisioned for Chatswood CBD and contained in the Chatswood CBD Planning and Urban Design Strategy 2036.

## Controls

- The building setbacks are to be in accordance with Map 5 (Setbacks and street frontage heights) and the concept plans. Setbacks are as follows:
- Anderson Street frontage:
- Minimum 6m setback at ground Level
- Minimum 6.4m setback above street wall
- Maximum street wall height of 7m or two storeys.
- O'Brien Street frontage:

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 123 -->


## Willoughby Development Control Plan Part L: Place Based Plans 2023

- Minimum 1.15m setback at ground Level
- Minimum 4.35m setback above street wall
- Maximum street wall height of 7m or two storeys.
- Day Street frontage:
- Nil setback at ground Level
- Minimum 4.5m above street wall
- Maximum street wall height of 7m or two storeys.
- Western (rear publicly accessible pathway) boundary
- Minimum 2m setback at ground Level, with additional stepped 2m setback at Podium Level
- Minimum 7.6m setback above street wall
- Maximum wall height to rear pathway of 7m or two storeys.
- In addition to Control 1:
- Setbacks may be greater and street wall heights may be lower.
- Additional ground level setbacks are sought that contribute to public realm.
![page 123 img 1 (904x704)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0069-e1337ebbcb36.png)


*Map 5: Setbacks and street frontage height*


<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 124 -->


# 5. Building Exterior


## Performance Criteria

- Buildings are to demonstrate a high design quality when viewed from the public domain and the surrounding area, including the eastern side of Anderson Street and the publicly accessible pathway to the western boundary.
- Facade treatment and design is to be used to break down the mass and bulk of buildings.
- High quality façade materials and finishes are to be used which contribute positively to the built environment and mitigate urban heat.

## Controls

- Facades are to be articulated and should incorporate recesses and projecting elements that do not encroach into required setbacks.
- Extensive blank walls shall be avoided at street level.

# 6. Amenity


## Performance Criteria

- Maximise solar access and ventilation to residential units.
- Ensure visual and acoustic privacy of residential units in the development and adjoining properties.
- Improve pedestrian amenity surrounding the site.

## Controls

- A Wind Assessment shall be submitted at Development Application Stage.
- A detailed Acoustic Assessment shall be submitted at Development Application Stage.
- Residential units shall be designed to maximize solar access, cross ventilation, visual and acoustic privacy.

# 7. Open Space and Landscaping


## Performance Criteria

- Landscaping is to soften and complement the development.
- Landscaping at street level shall improve the amenity and appearance of the pedestrian environment.
- The development shall provide publicly accessible links and open space.
- Publicly accessible open space is to include meaningful green landscaping.
- Greening at the podium roof level is to be provided, with planting visible to the surrounding area - with particular regard to Anderson Street, O'Brien Street, Day Street and the western boundary with the publicly accessible pathway.
- Podium and roof tops are to be a combination of green and recreation spaces.
- Street tree planting is to be provided.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 125 -->


## Controls

- Open space at ground level shall be utilised as publicly accessible open space.
- All roofs up to 30 metres from ground are to be green roofs. These are to provide a balance of passive and active green spaces that maximize solar access.
- A minimum of 2 hours of sun access is to be provided to the public open space on the site.
- Public domain improvements shall be provided to all street frontages to Council requirements.
- A minimum of 20% of the site is to be provided as soft landscaping, which may be located on ground, podium and roof top levels or green walls of buildings.
- Deep soil planting is to be provided within the 6m setback to Anderson Street. Deep soil plantings include trees and shrubs, and are to be unimpeded by buildings or structures below ground.
- A Landscape Plan is to be provided at Development Application stage detailing all public domain at ground level, street tree planting, planting and space allocation at podium and roof top levels. This is to include species, container size at planting, spacing and approximate size at maturity.
- Large canopy tree planting must be provided along the Anderson Street frontage within the 3m setback.
- Street tree planting is at the cost of the proponent, with location and species to be determined in consultation with Council at Development Application stage.
- All existing aerial cables which may include for electricity, communications and other cables connecting to street poles and buildings around the site shall be removed and installed underground in accordance with the requirements of the relevant service authorities. Ausgrid lighting poles are to be provided to the requirements of Ausgrid for street lighting and shall be positioned compatible to the landscaping design around the site.

# 8. Links


## Performance Criteria

- The development shall provide publicly accessible through site links and open space.
- Publicly accessible open space is to include green landscaping.

## Controls

- The development is to incorporate publicly accessible through site links and open space in accordance with Map 4 below. In this regard a 2m wide publicly accessible through site link is required along the western boundary, adjacent the existing publicly accessible pathway. This space is to function as a landscape embellishment to the existing publicly accessible pathway.
- Through site links and open space in addition to Map 4 is required on a site by site basis.
- Public rights of way are to be provided on:
- The 6m setback to Anderson Street

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 126 -->

- The 1.15m setback to O'Brien Street
- The 2m setback to the western boundary with the adjacent existing publicly accessible pathway.
- All publicly accessible open space and links are to be the responsibility of the relevant ownership entity, with formal public access to be created over these areas.
![page 126 img 1 (940x760)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0081-865796cce836.png)


*Map 4: Through Site Links and Open Space*


# 9. Active Street Frontages


## Performance Criteria

- To ensure that uses on the ground level contribute to the activation of the public domain.
- To ensure that design and location of ground floor uses maximize surveillance of the public domain.

## Controls

- At ground level buildings are to maximise active frontages to Anderson Street, O'Brien Street and Day Street.
- A building has an active street frontage if all premises on the ground floor of the building facing the street(s) are used for the purpose of commercial premises or non-residential purposes and provide elements of visual interest when viewed from the street.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 127 -->


# 10. Traffic and Transport


## Performance Criteria

- Development must be designed to provide adequate and safe access to the site.
- Development on the site should not cause adverse traffic impacts on the surrounding road system.
- Minimise the number of vehicular access points to the development.
- All vehicles are to enter and exit the site in a forward direction.
- Traffic and transport solutions are to be physical (rather than mechanical) on this site.
- Minimise car parking and encourage alternative transport options.

## Controls

- Vehicle access to / egress from the development is to be from one access point in Day Street.
- Vehicle access and egress is to be designed and located to achieve safety, minimise conflicts between pedestrians and vehicles and create a high quality streetscape.
- All car parking and loading facilities are to be located below ground level.
- Other strategies for car parking reduction, such as reciprocal arrangements for sharing parking and car share, is to be included in any future Development Application.
- The following is to be provided in any future development application:
- Car parking provision based on a reduced car parking rate, consistent with the requirements of SEPP65 / constrained parking rates for new developments in the Chatswood CBD as supported by Transport for NSW (TfNSW).
- A minimum of 1 secure bicycle parking space per apartment.
- A minimum of 1 secure bicycle space per 100m² of non-residential /retail floor space.
- Adequate end of trip facilities including lockers, showers, etc. for use by nonresidential and retail tenants.
- A bicycle rack within the site boundary for use by retail customers.
- A minimum of three (3) freight and service vehicle spaces within the basement, in addition to the one (1) Medium Rigid Vehicle (MRV) space proposed within basement level 1 loading dock.
- Evidence of consultation between the proponent and Sydney Trains, and any conclusions, to ensure that all relevant Sydney Trains matters of consideration are taken into account and are incorporated in the future design of the development.
- A Green Travel Plan.
- Updated traffic analysis and modelling.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 128 -->

## Performance Criteria

- All loading, unloading and servicing is required to occur on-site.
- To ensure that adequate provision is made for waste storage and disposal.
- Floor space at ground level is to be maximised, with services located in basement.

## Controls

- All loading and unloading services are required to occur at basement level on-site.
- Other supporting functions such as garbage rooms, plant and other services are to be located in basement levels.
- A Waste Management Plan shall be submitted at the Development Application stage.
- Substations are to be provided within buildings, not within the streets, open spaces or setbacks and not facing key active street frontages. Substations are to be designed to ensure protection of residents from Electro Magnetic Radiation (EMR) emissions.

# 12. Design Excellence


## Performance Criteria

- Ensure high quality and varied design through the use of competitive design processes.
- Implement a rigorous process to support good design outcomes.

## Controls

- All developments that have a height of 35m or more are subject to a competitive design process.
- The competitive design process must be undertaken in accordance with the Willoughby Design Excellence Policy and Willoughby Design Excellence Guidelines.

# 13. Public Art


## Performance Criteria

- All redevelopments in the Chatswood CBD should contribute to public art in accordance with Council's Public Art Policy.

## Controls

- Public Art is to be provided in accordance with Council's Public Art Policy.

# 14. Building Sustainability


## Performance Criteria

- Design excellence shall include achievement of higher building sustainability standards.

## Controls

- A minimum of 5 stars GBCA building rating is required. A higher rating is encouraged. An assessment report is to be submitted at Development Application stage.

- The building setbacks are to be in accordance with Map 5 (Setbacks and street frontage heights) - except where additional setback is provided. Setbacks are as follows:
- Pacific Highway frontage
- Minimum 4m setback at ground Level
- ii) Minimum 6m setback above street wall
- iii) Maximum street wall height of 7m or two storeys.
- Gordon Avenue frontage:

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 141 -->

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part L: Place Based Plans 2023

- Nil setback at ground Level
- ii) Minimum 3m setback above street wall
- iii) Maximum street wall height of 6-14m (two to four storeys).
- Hammond Lane frontage
- Minimum 3m setback at ground Level
- ii) Minimum 6m setback above street wall
- iii) Maximum street wall height of 6-14m (two to four storeys).
- Southern boundary with adjoining property
- Nil setback at ground Level
- ii) Minimum 6m setback above street wall
- In addition to Control 1:
- Setbacks may be greater and street wall heights may be lower.
- Additional ground level setbacks are sought that contribute to public realm.
![page 141 img 1 (576x448)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0087-faaf9ee099d2.png)


*Map 5: Setbacks and street frontage heights*


<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 142 -->


# 5. Building Exterior


## Performance Criteria

- Buildings are to demonstrate a high design quality when viewed from the public domain and the surrounding area, including Pacific Highway, Gordon Avenue and Hammond Lane.
- Facade treatment and design is to be used to break down the mass and bulk of buildings.
- High quality façade materials and finishes are to be used which contribute positively to the built environment and mitigate urban heat.

## Controls

- Facades are to be articulated and should incorporate recesses and projecting elements that do not encroach into required setbacks.
- Extensive blank walls shall be avoided at street level.

# 6. Amenity


## Performance Criteria

- Maximise solar access and ventilation to residential units.
- Ensure visual and acoustic privacy of residential units in the development and adjoining properties.
- Improve pedestrian amenity surrounding the site.

## Controls

- A Wind Assessment shall be submitted at Development Application Stage.
- A detailed Acoustic Assessment shall be submitted at Development Application Stage.
- Residential units shall be designed to maximize solar access, cross ventilation, visual and acoustic privacy.

# 7. Open Space and Landscaping


## Performance Criteria

- Landscaping is to soften and complement the development.
- Landscaping at street level shall improve the amenity and appearance of the pedestrian environment.
- The development shall provide publicly accessible links and open space.
- Publicly accessible open space is to include meaningful green landscaping.
- Greening at the podium roof level is to be provided, with planting visible to the surrounding area - with particular regard to Pacific Highway, Gordon Avenue and Hammond Lane.
- Podium and roof tops are to be a combination of green and recreation spaces.
- Street tree planting is to be provided.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 143 -->


## Controls

- Open space at ground level shall be utilised as publicly accessible open space.
- Large canopy tree planting must be provided along the Pacific Highway frontage within the 4m setback area.
- All roofs up to 30 metres from ground are to be green roofs. These are to provide a balance of passive and active green spaces that maximize solar access.
- A minimum of 2 hours of sun access is to be provided to the public open space on the site.
- Public domain improvements shall be provided to all street frontages to Council requirements.
- A minimum of 20% of the site is to be provided as soft landscaping, which may be located on ground, podium and roof top levels or green walls of buildings.
- Deep soil planting is to be provided within the 4m setback to Pacific Highway. Deep soil plantings include trees and shrubs, and are to be unimpeded by buildings or structures below ground.
- A Landscape Plan is to be provided at Development Application stage detailing all public domain at ground level, street tree planting, planting and space allocation at podium and roof top levels. This is to include species, container size at planting, spacing and approximate size at maturity.
- Street tree planting is at the cost of the proponent, with location and species to be determined in consultation with Council at Development Application stage.
- All existing aerial cables which may include for electricity, communications and other cables connecting to street poles and buildings around the site shall be removed and installed underground in accordance with the requirements of the relevant service authorities. Ausgrid lighting poles are to be provided to the requirements of Ausgrid for street lighting and shall be positioned compatible to the landscaping design around the site.

# 8. Links


## Performance Criteria

- The development shall provide publicly accessible through site links and open space.
- Publicly accessible open space is to include green landscaping.

## Controls

- The development is to incorporate publicly accessible through site links and open space in accordance with Map 4 below.
- Through site links and open space in addition to Map 4 is required on a site by site basis.
- Public rights of way are to be provided on:
- The 4m setback to Pacific Highway.
- The 3m setback to Hammond Lane.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 144 -->

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part L: Place Based Plans 2023

- All publicly accessible open space and links are to be the responsibility of the relevant ownership entity, with formal public access to be created over these areas.
- The Hammond Lane setback is to be integrated with the through site link at 613-627 Pacific Highway, Chatswood.
![page 144 img 1 (602x487)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0135-d805815570d2.png)


*Map 4 : Through Site Links and Open Space*


# 9. Active Street Frontages


## Performance Criteria

- To ensure that uses on the ground level contribute to the activation of the public domain.
- To ensure that design and location of ground floor uses maximize surveillance of the public domain.

## Controls

- At ground level buildings are to maximise active frontages to Pacific Highway, Gordon Avenue and Hammond Lane.
- A building has an active street frontage if all premises on the ground floor of the building facing the street(s) are used for the purpose of commercial premises or non-residential purposes and provide elements of visual interest when viewed from the street.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 145 -->


# 10. Traffic and Transport


## Performance Criteria

- Development must be designed to provide adequate and safe access to the site.
- Development on the site should not cause adverse traffic impacts on the surrounding road system.
- Minimise the number of vehicular access points to the development.
- All vehicles are to enter and exit the site in a forward direction.
- Traffic and transport solutions are to be physical (rather than mechanical) on this site.
- Minimise car parking and encourage alternative transport options.

## Controls

- Vehicle and loading access is to be reviewed and master planned in conjunction with the adjoining site at 613-627 Pacific Highway, Chatswood. One vehicle and loading point in Hammond Lane is preferred for the accessing and servicing of 629-637 Pacific Highway and 613-627 Pacific Highway, via a consolidated basement.
- Vehicle access and egress is to be designed and located to achieve safety, minimise conflicts between pedestrians and vehicles and create a high quality streetscape.
- All car parking and loading facilities are to be located below ground level.
- Other strategies for car parking reduction, such as reciprocal arrangements for sharing parking and car share, is to be included in any future Development Application.
- The following is to be provided in any future development application:
- Car parking provision based on reduced car parking rates, consistent with the requirements for new developments in the Chatswood CBD as supported by Transport for NSW.
- A minimum of 1 secure bicycle parking space per apartment.
- A minimum of 1 secure bicycle space per 100m² of non-residential /retail floor space.
- Adequate end of trip facilities including lockers, showers, etc. for use by non-residential and retail tenants.
- A bicycle rack within the site boundary for use by retail customers.
- A minimum of three (3) freight and service vehicle spaces within the basement, in addition to the one (1) Medium Rigid Vehicle (MRV) space proposed within the loading dock.
- A Green Travel Plan.
- Updated traffic analysis and modelling.

# 11. Waste Management, Loading and Services


## Performance Criteria

- All loading, unloading and servicing is required to occur on-site.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 146 -->

Willoughby Development Control Plan Part L: Place Based Plans 2023

- To ensure that adequate provision is made for waste storage and disposal.
- Floor space at ground level is to be maximised, with services located in basement.

## Controls

- All loading and unloading services are required to occur at basement level on-site.
- Other supporting functions such as garbage rooms, plant and other services are to be located in basement levels.
- A Waste Management Plan shall be submitted at the Development Application stage.
- Substations are to be provided within buildings, not within the streets, open spaces or setbacks and not facing key active street frontages. Substations are to be designed to ensure protection of residents from Electro Magnetic Radiation (EMR) emissions.

# 12. Design Excellence


## Performance Criteria

- Ensure high quality and varied design through the use of competitive design processes.
- Implement a rigorous process to support good design outcomes.

## Controls

- All developments that have a height of 35m or more are subject to a competitive design process.
- The competitive design process must be undertaken in accordance with the Willoughby Design Excellence Policy and Willoughby Design Excellence Guidelines.

# 13. Public Art


## Performance Criteria

- All redevelopments in the Chatswood CBD should contribute to public art in accordance with Council's Public Art Policy.

## Controls

- Public Art is to be provided in accordance with Council's Public Art Policy.

# 14. Building Sustainability


## Performance Criteria

- Design excellence shall include achievement of higher building sustainability standards.

## Controls

- A minimum of 5 stars GBCA building rating is required. A higher rating is encouraged. An assessment report is to be submitted at Development Application stage.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 147 -->

- All existing aerial cables which may include for electricity, communications and other cables connecting to street poles and buildings around the site shall be removed and installed underground in accordance with the requirements of the relevant service authorities. Ausgrid lighting poles are to be provided to the requirements of Ausgrid for street lighting and shall be positioned compatible to the landscaping design around the site.

# 8. Links


## Performance Criteria

- The development shall provide publicly accessible through site links and open space.
- Publicly accessible open space is to include green landscaping.

## Controls

- The development is to incorporate publicly accessible through site links and open space in accordance with Map 4 below.
- Through site links and open space in addition to Map 4 is required on a site by site basis.
- Public rights of way are to be provided on:
- The 3m setback to Gordon Avenue.
- The 3m setback to Nelson Street.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 162 -->

- The 3m setback along the eastern boundary (from Gordon Avenue to Nelson Street) - adjacent the Frank Channon Walk and the pocket park at the end of Gordon Avenue.
- All publicly accessible open space and links are to be the responsibility of the relevant ownership entity, with formal public access to be created over these areas.
![page 162 img 1 (602x487)](images/willoughby-development-control-plan-2023/p0135-d805815570d2.png)


*Map 4: Through Site Links and Open Space*


# 9. Active Street Frontages


## Performance Criteria

- To ensure that uses on the ground level contribute to the activation of the public domain.
- To ensure that design and location of ground floor uses maximize surveillance of the public domain.

## Controls

- At ground level buildings are to maximise active frontages to Gordon Avenue and Nelson Street.
- A building has an active street frontage if all premises on the ground floor of the building facing the street(s) are used for the purpose of commercial premises or non-residential purposes and provide elements of visual interest when viewed from the street.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 163 -->


# 10. Traffic and Transport


## Performance Criteria

- Development must be designed to provide adequate and safe access to the site.
- Development on the site should not cause adverse traffic impacts on the surrounding road system.
- Minimise the number of vehicular access points to the development.
- All vehicles are to enter and exit the site in a forward direction.
- Traffic and transport solutions are to be physical (rather than mechanical) on this site.
- Minimise car parking and encourage alternative transport options.

## Controls

- Vehicle and loading access is to be reviewed and master planned in conjunction with the adjoining land at 10 Gordon Avenue and 15-19 Nelson Street. One vehicle and loading point in Gordon Avenue is preferred for the block bounded by Nelson Street, Gordon Avenue, Hammond Lane and the Frank Channon Walk, via a consolidated basement.
- Vehicle access and egress is to be designed and located to achieve safety, minimise conflicts between pedestrians and vehicles and create a high quality streetscape.
- All car parking and loading facilities are to be located below ground level, utilizing physical solutions to ensure all vehicles (including loading vehicles) enter and leave the site in a forward direction.
- Other strategies for car parking reduction, such as reciprocal arrangements for sharing parking and car share, is to be included in any future Development Application.
- The following is to be provided in any future development application:
- Car parking provision based on reduced car parking rates, consistent with the requirements for new developments in the Chatswood CBD as supported by Transport for NSW.
- A minimum of 1 secure bicycle parking space per apartment.
- A minimum of 1 secure bicycle space per 100m² of non-residential /retail floor space.
- Adequate end of trip facilities including lockers, showers, etc. for use by nonresidential and retail tenants.
- A bicycle rack within the site boundary for use by retail customers.
- A minimum of three (3) freight and service vehicle spaces within the basement, in addition to the one (1) Medium Rigid Vehicle (MRV) space proposed within the loading dock.
- A Green Travel Plan.
- Updated traffic analysis and modelling.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 164 -->


# 11. Waste Management, Loading and Services


## Performance Criteria

- All loading, unloading and servicing is required to occur on-site.
- To ensure that adequate provision is made for waste storage and disposal.
- Floor space at ground level is to be maximised, with services located in basement.

## Controls

- All loading and unloading services are required to occur at basement level on-site.
- Other supporting functions such as garbage rooms, plant and other services are to be located in basement levels.
- A Waste Management Plan shall be submitted at the Development Application stage.
- Substations are to be provided within buildings, not within the streets, open spaces or setbacks and not facing key active street frontages. Substations are to be designed to ensure protection of residents from Electro Magnetic Radiation (EMR) emissions.

# 12. Design Excellence


## Performance Criteria

- Ensure high quality and varied design through the use of competitive design processes.
- Implement a rigorous process to support good design outcomes.

## Controls

- All developments that have a height of 35m or more are subject to a competitive design process
- The competitive design process must be undertaken in accordance with the Willoughby Design Excellence Policy and Willoughby Design Excellence Guidelines.

# 13. Public Art


## Performance Criteria

- All redevelopments in the Chatswood CBD should contribute to public art in accordance with Council's Public Art Policy.

## Controls

- Public Art is to be provided in accordance with Council's Public Art Policy.

# 14. Building Sustainability


## Performance Criteria

- Design excellence shall include achievement of higher building sustainability standards.

## Controls

- A minimum of 5 stars GBCA building rating is required. A higher rating is encouraged. An assessment report is to be submitted at Development Application stage.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 165 -->

- Ensure development on the site minimises impacts to the amenity of neighbouring residential properties.

- Achieve a site layout that provides a pleasant environment for the occupants and minimises impact on surrounding properties.
- Ensure visual and acoustic privacy, natural ventilation, sun access, and views.
- Provide suitable areas for communal open spaces, deep soil zones, and landscaping.

## Controls

- Be consistent with the permitted Height of Buildings development standard applicable to the site.
- Minimise overshadowing of surrounding properties, key public spaces and public domain.

## Controls

- The maximum building height is to include all structures located at roof level, including lift over runs and any other architectural features.
- All roof top lift over runs or exposed structures are to be integrated with the building.
- Flat roof areas shall incorporate useable outdoor recreation space where suitable, within the maximum building height.

- Contribute to slender tower forms.
- Minimise the effects of adverse wind conditions at street level.

# 5. Building Exterior


## Performance Criteria

- Buildings are to demonstrate a high design quality when viewed from the public domain and the surrounding area, including Pacific Highway, O'Brien Street, Wilson Street and the pocket park and through site link between O'Brien and Wilson Street, adjacent the North Shore Rail Line.
- Facade treatment and design is to be used to break down the mass and bulk of buildings.
- High quality façade materials and finishes are to be used which contribute positively to the built environment and mitigate urban heat.

## Controls

- Facades are to be articulated and should incorporate recesses and projecting elements that do not encroach into required setbacks.
- Extensive blank walls shall be avoided at street level.

# 6. Amenity


## Performance Criteria

- Maximise solar access and ventilation to residential units.
- Ensure visual and acoustic privacy of residential units in the development and adjoining properties.
- Improve pedestrian amenity surrounding the site.

## Controls

- A Wind Assessment shall be submitted at Development Application Stage.
- A detailed Acoustic Assessment shall be submitted at Development Application Stage addressing noise and vibrations from both the Pacific Highway and the North Shore Rail Line.
- Residential units shall be designed to maximize solar access, cross ventilation, visual and acoustic privacy.

# 7. Open Space and Landscaping


## Performance Criteria

- Landscaping is to soften and complement the development.
- Landscaping at street level shall improve the amenity and appearance of the pedestrian environment.
- The development shall provide publicly accessible links and open space.
- Publicly accessible open space is to include meaningful green landscaping.
- Greening at the podium roof level is to be provided, with planting visible to the surrounding area - with particular regard to Pacific Highway, O'Brien Street, Wilson Street and the pocket park and through site link between O'Brien and Wilson Streets, adjacent the North Shore Rail Line.

<!-- SRC: 11-part-l-place-based-plans.pdf | PAGE: 171 -->

- Podium and roof tops are to be a combination of green and recreation spaces.
- Street tree planting is to be provided.

## Controls

- Open space at ground level shall be utilised as publicly accessible open space.
- Large canopy tree planting must be provided along the Pacific Highway, O'Brien Street frontages, and the pocket park and through site link between O'Brien and Wilson Street, adjacent the North Shore Rail Line, where any setback area is greater than 3m.
- All roofs up to 30 metres from ground are to be green roofs. These are to provide a balance of passive and active green spaces that maximize solar access.
- A minimum of 2 hours of sun access is to be provided to the public open space on the site.
- Public domain improvements shall be provided to all street frontages, and the pocket park and through site link between O'Brien and Wilson Streets, adjacent the North Shore Rail Line, to Council requirements.
- A minimum of 20% of the site is to be provided as soft landscaping, which may be located on ground, podium and roof top levels or green walls of buildings.
- Deep soil planting is to be provided along the Pacific Highway, O'Brien Street frontages, and the pocket park and through site link between O'Brien and Wilson Streets, adjacent the North Shore Rail Line, where any setback area is greater than 3m. Deep soil plantings include trees and shrubs, and are to be unimpeded by buildings or structures below ground.
- A landscape plan is to be provided at Development Application stage detailing all public domain at ground level, street tree planting, planting and space allocation at podium and roof top levels. This is to include species, container size at planting, spacing and approximate size at maturity.
- Street tree planting is at the cost of the proponent, with location and species to be determined in consultation with Council at Development Application stage.
- All existing aerial cables which may include for electricity, communications and other cables connecting to street poles and buildings around the site shall be removed and installed underground in accordance with the requirements of the relevant service authorities. Ausgrid lighting poles are to be provided to the requirements of Ausgrid for street lighting and shall be positioned compatible to the landscaping design around the site.

- All publicly accessible open space and links are to be the responsibility of the relevant ownership entity, with formal public access to be created over these areas.
